text:
I bless thee  David in the Name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit! Amen!
Heavenly Father, I lift this beloved one into Your loving hands, asking that Your healing touch restore his body completely. Remove all heart problems, leukemia, cancer, disease, infirmary, injury, sickness, fatigue, or pain, and renew his strength, energy, and vitality. Grant wisdom and skill to the medical team, patience to this beloved one, and peace to his heart. Surround him with Your divine protection, and let Your presence comfort and reassure him. May Your grace and mercy flow through every part David’s being. In Jesus’ name I beg and pray, Amen.

Prayer to the Holy Spirit:
Come, Holy Spirit, Divine Comforter and Breath of Life. Enter all places of heart problems, cancer, tumors, pain, injury, disease, infection, suffering, weakness and fear. Remove every and all infirmary, and surround  David with Your gentle light, while completely healing  David while filling his heart with the strength and peace that comes from above, trusting to the power of God’s eternal love. Amen.

Pray to the Blessed Holy Mother Mary:

Dear Mother Mary, With hearts heavy and bodies burdened, we approach your divine presence, seeking your miraculous touch. Your healing power knows no equal, and in our times of need, we implore you to mend not only our physical wounds but the scars that mar our souls. Pour forth your divine grace upon us, dear Mother, and restore us to a state of wholeness, that we may bear witness to the miracle of your love. Amen.

Prayer to St. Jude:

Oh glorious apostle St. Jude, faithful servant and friend of Jesus, the name of the traitor who delivered thy beloved Master into the hands of His enemies has caused thee to be forgotten by many, but the Church honors and invokes thee universally as the patron of hopeless cases--of things despaired of. Pray for me who am so miserable; make use, I implore thee, of that particular privilege accorded thee of bringing visible and speedy help where help is almost despaired of. Come to my assistance in this great need, that I may receive the consolations and succor of heaven in all my necessities, tribulations and sufferings, particularly—completely heal from all heart problems, injuries, cancer and diseases, and protect David —and that I may bless God with thee and all the elect throughout eternity. I promise thee, O blessed St. Jude, to be ever mindful of this great favor, and I will never cease to honor thee as my special and powerful patron, and to do all in my power to encourage devotion to thee. Amen

Prayer to St. Michael (Long Version)

O Glorious Prince of the heavenly host, Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in the battle and fearful warfare that we are waging against the principalities and powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the evil spirits. Come thou to the assistance of men, whom Almighty God created immortal, making them in His own image and likeness and redeeming them at a great price from the tyranny of Satan. Fight this day the battle of the Lord with thy legions of holy Angels, even as of old thou didst fight against Lucifer, the leader of the proud spirits and all his rebel angels, who were powerless to stand against thee, neither was their place found any more in heaven. And that great dragon was cast forth, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and satan, who seduces the whole world; and he was cast forth upon Earth, and his angels were sent with him.

But behold! the ancient enemy of mankind and a murderer from the beginning has been fiercely aroused. Changing himself into an angel of light, he goes about with the whole multitude of the wicked spirits to invade the earth and blot out the Name of God and of His Christ, to plunder, to slay, and to consign to eternal damnation the souls that have been destined for a crown of everlasting life. This wicked serpent, like an unclean torrent, pours into men of depraved minds and corrupt hearts the poison of his malice, the spirit of lying, impiety and blasphemy, and the deadly breath of impurity and every form of vice and iniquity.

Be favorable to Thy Church, the Bride of the Lamb without spot, whose enemies have filled to overflowing with gall and inebriated with wormwood. They have laid profane hands upon Her most sacred treasures. Where the See of the most blessed Peter and the Chair of Truth has been constituted as a light to the nations, there they have placed a throne of their abomination and impiety; so that with the Pastor struck, they may prevail to disperse the flock.

Therefore, most invincible Leader, be with the people of God against this spiritual wickedness and bring about victory. Thou art venerated by Holy Church as Her guard and patron; Thou art glorified as our defender against the impious powers of earth and of hell. Unto thee the Lord hath handed over the souls of the redeemed to be placed in happiness above.

Entreat the God of peace, to obliterate satan beneath our feet, lest he prevail further to hold men captive, and to injure the Church. Offer our prayers in the sight of the Most High, so that the mercy of the Lord may swiftly overtake us, and apprehend the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and satan, and send him bound into the abyss, so that he may seduce the nations no more.

Henceforth having been confided to thy escort and protection, we sacred ministers by the authority of the Holy Mother Church [if recited by a cleric of the order of exorcist or above, say instead: by our authority], do undertake to repel the infestations of diabolical deceit in the Name of Jesus Christ, Our God and Lord.

Behold the Cross of the Lord; be scattered hostile powers.
The Lion of the tribe of Juda has conquered, the root of David.
Let Thy mercies be upon us, O Lord.
As we have hoped in Thee.
O Lord, hear my prayer.
And let my cry come unto Thee.
The Lord be with you all.
And with thy spirit.

Let us pray.
O God, and Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ, we invoke Thy Holy Name, and we humbly implore Thy clemency so that, through the intercession of Mary, the Immaculate ever-Virgin Mother of God, of blessed Michael the Archangel, of blessed Joseph, the Spouse of the same blessed Virgin, of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints, Thou may deign to offer us aid against satan, and all the other unclean spirits, who wander through the world to injure the human race and to destroy souls. We ask this through Christ Our Lord. Amen.

Prayer for possible any evil influence:

In His Name and by the power of His Cross and Blood, I ask Jesus Christ to bind any evil spirits, forces and powers of the earth, air, fire, water, and of the netherworld and all of the satanic forces of nature. By the power of the Holy Spirit and by His authority, I ask Jesus Christ to break any and all curses, hexes, vexes, jinks, spells, and all wrong prayers and words, and to send them all back to where they came from, if it be His Holy Will. I beseech Thee, Lord Jesus Christ, to protect us by pouring Thy Precious Blood on us; myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for; which Thou hast shed for us and I ask Thee to command that any departing spirits leave quietly, without disturbance, and go straight to Thy Cross to be disposed of as Thou sees fit. I ask Thee to bind any demonic interactions, interplay, or communications. I place myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for, and all things I pray and intercede for under the protection of the Blood of Jesus Christ which He has shed for us. Amen.

Prayer for Surgery (In case needed.)

Lord Almighty, I lift up this beloved one David, as they face surgery. Protect them, guide the hands of doctors and nurses, and grant wisdom in every decision. Remove fear, anxiety, and complications, replacing them with Your peace and assurance. Restore their health, strength, and vitality quickly, and surround them with Your loving presence. Comfort their heart, strengthen their spirit, and let Your healing flow through David’s body. May they recover fully, trusting Your mercy and experiencing Your grace throughout this trial. Amen.

text:
THE MESSAGES OF LA SALETTE: MAXIM.
.
"On the 19th of September, 1846, I saw a lady brilliant like the sun, whom I believe to be the Holy Virgin. However, I have never said it was the Holy Virgin. I have always said that I saw a lady, but never ventured to affirm that it was the Holy Virgin."
.
"From what I am going to state here, it appertains to the Church to judge whether it was truly the Holy Virgin or some other person. She gave me my secret about the middle of Her conversation with me, after these words: 'The grapes shall rot, and the chestnuts shall be bad.' The Lady began by saying to me:
.
"1. 'Three fourths of France shall  lose the faith, and the other
fourth,  that will preserve it, will practice it with tepidity.
"2. Peace shall not be given to the world until men will be
converted.
"3. 'A Protestant nation in the North shall be converted to the
faith, and through the means of that nation, the others shall return to the Holy  Catholic Church.
"4. 'The next Pope shall not be a Roman.
"5. 'When men shall be converted, God will give peace to the
world.
"6. 'Afterwards this peace shall be disturbed by the monster.
"7. 'The monster shall arrive at the end of this nineteenth
century or, at latest, at the commencement of the twentieth.
"8. 'In this time the Antichrist will be born of a nun of Hebraic
descent, a false virgin, who will have intercourse with the ancient
serpent, with the master of impurity and putrefaction. His father will be a bishop. He will perform false miracles and subsist only on vitiating faith. He will have his brethren, who will be children of evil but not incarnate devils like himself. Soon they will be at the head of armies, supported by the Legions of Hell.
"9. 'Up, ye children of light, and fight or behold, the age of ages, the  end, the extremity is at hand! The Church passes into
darkness. The  world will be in a state of consternation, perplexity and confusion.
"10. 'Enoch and Elias, they will suddenly appear on earth full
of the Spirit of God, when the Church becomes darkened and the world in terrible agony. They will convert those of good will and comfort the oppressed Christians. With the help of the Holy Ghost, they will have great success against the heresies of the Antichrist. But in the end they will be delivered unto death.' "
-----------------------------------------------
MELANIE.
.
Melanie's secret  message, which follows, was published in its entirety in a brochure which she had publish in 1879 at Lecce, Italy, with the approval of the Bishop of Lecce.
.
The Lady said to me:
.
What I shall tell you now will not always remain a secret. You are allowed to publish it after the year 1858.
.
There will be a kind of false peace before the advent of Antichrist. Man's only thought will be upon diversions and amusements. The wicked will indulge in all sorts of sin, but the children of the Holy Church, the children of the faith, my Sincere followers, will wax strong in the love of God and in the virtues that are dear to Me. Happy the humble souls that are guided by the Holy Ghost.
I will fight with them until they shall have reached the completion of age.
.
"Italy will be severely punished for her efforts to shake off the yoke of the Most High Lord. She will become the play-ball Of war. On every side blood will flow. The temples will either be closed or desecrated. Priests and members of Religious orders will be put to flight. They will be beaten to death and otherwise die cruel deaths.
.
"The Vicar of My Son will be compelled to suffer much because for a time the Church will be delivered to great persecutions: That will be the hour of darkness, and the Church will experience a frightful crisis. The  powerful officials of the state and the Church will be suppressed and done away with, and all law and order as well as justice.
.
There will be  murder, hate, envy and deceit, with no love or regard for one's country or family.
.
"God is going to punish in a manner without example. Woe to the  inhabitants of the earth! God is going to exhaust his wrath, and nobody shall be able to evade so many combined evils. At the first stroke of His  fulminating sword the mountains and the whole of nature shall shake with terror, use the disorders and crimes of men pierce the very Vaults of the Heavens. The earth shall be stricken with every kind of plagues. [Besides the pestilence and famine, which shall be general.]
.
There shall  be wars until the last war, which shall be waged by the ten kings of Antichrist. All these Kings shall a common design, and they only shall  govern the world.
.
Priests and Religious shall be hunted; they shall be butchered in a cruel manner. Many shall abandon the Faith, and great shall be the number of Priests and Religious who shall separate themselves from the True Religion; among these there will be found likewise several bishops.
.
Let the Pope be upon his guard against miracle workers, for the time is arrived when the most astounding prodigies will take place on the earth and in the air.
.
"Lucifer, with a very great number of demons will be unchained from Hell. By degrees they shall abolish the Faith, even among persons consecrated to God. They shall blind them in such a manner that, without very special graces, these persons shall imbibe the spirit of those wicked angels. Many religious houses will entirely lose the Faith, and shall be the cause of the loss of many persons. The Superiors of Religious Communities should be alert regarding the ones they take into the community, for the devil will use all malice, to bring persons into the Orders who are addicted to sin.
.
"Bad people will abound upon the earth; and the spirit, of darkness shall spread over the earth a universal relaxation about everything relating to the Service of God. Satan shall have very great power over nature [God's punishment for the crimes of men]; temples will be erected for the worship of these demons. Some persons shall be transported from one place to another by these wicked spirits, even some priests, because these will not be animated by the Holy Spirit of the Gospel, which is a spirit of humility, charity, and zeal for the Glory of God.
.
"Some will make the dead rise and appear as holy persons. The souls of the dammed shall also be summoned, and shall appear as united to their bodies. Such persons, resurrected through the agency of demons, shall assume the figure of holy persons, who are known to have been upon earth, in order more easily to deceive them. These self-styled resuscitated persons shall be nothing but demons under their forms. In this way they shall preach a Gospel contrary to that of Jesus Christ, denying the existence of Heaven.
.
"In every place there shall be seen extraordinary prodigies, because the True Faith has been extinguished, and a pale light shines in the world.
.
"My sons Vicar shall have much to suffer, because for a time the Church shall be exposed to very great persecutions. It shall be the time of darkness. The Church shall have to pass through an awful crisis. France, Italy, Spain, and England shall have Civil War. Blood shall flow through the streets. French shall fight French. Italians against Italians. After this there will be a frightful general war. For a time God shall not remember France, nor Italy [for two years or for one?] because the Gospel of Jesus Christ is no more understood. The Holy Father will suffer much. I will be with him to the end to receive his sacrifice. The  wicked shall many times attempt his life.
.
" Nature demands vengeance against men, and she trembles with fright in expectation to what will befall the earth sullied with crimes. Tremble, O earth! And tremble you also who make profession of serving Jesus Christ, but inwardly worship yourselves because God has delivered  you to his enemies, because corruption is in holy places.
.
"In the year 1865 the abomination shall be seen in Holy Places, in Convents, and then the demon shall make himself as the king of hearts. It will be about that time that Antichrist shall be born. At his birth he shall vomit blasphemies. He shall have teeth; in a word, he shall be like an incarnate demon; he shall utter frightful screams; he shall work prodigies; and he shall feed on impure things. He shall have brothers who though not incarnate demons like him, shall nevertheless be children of iniquity. At the age of twelve years they shall have become remarkable for valiant victories, which they shall achieve; very soon each of them will be at the head of armies. Paris shall be burned, and  Marseilles shall be submerged; many great cities shall be shattered and swallowed up by earthquakes. The populace will believe that everything is lost, will see nothing but murder, and will hear only the clang of arms and sacrilegious blasphemies.
.
''I address a pressing appeal to the earth. I call upon the true Disciples of the Living God, Who reigns in the Heavens; I call upon the True Imitators of Christ made Man, the Only true Savior of mankind; I call upon My children, those who are truly devoted to Me, those who have offered themselves to me that I may lead them to My Son, those whom I carry as it were in My arms, those who have been animated by My Spirit. Finally, I call on the Apostles of these Last Days, these faithful Disciples of Jesus Christ, who have lived despising the world and themselves, in poverty and humility, in contempt and in, I silence, in prayer and mortification in chastity and union with God, in suffering and unknown to the world. It is time for them to come out and enlighten the World. Go ye forth and manifest yourselves as My darling children; I am with you and within you, so that your Faith may be light which
illumines You in these unhappy days, and that your zeal may make you long for the Glory and Honor of the Most High. Fight, ye children of light; combat, ye small band that can see, for this is the time of times, the end of ends.
.
"The seasons of the year will change, the earth will produce only bad fruits, the stars will depart from their regular course, the moon will give only a weak, reddish light. Water and fire in the interior of the earth will rage violently and cause terrible earthquakes, whereby mountains and cities will sink into the depths. Earthquakes will also devour whole countries. Together with the Antichrist the demons will work great false miracles on earth and in the air. Voices will be heard in the air. Then men will desert Religion and become worse and worse. Men will let themselves be deceived because they refused to adore the real Christ Who lives bodily amongst them. Woe to the inhabitants of the earth. Bloody wars, famines pestilence and contagious diseases will develop. Terrible rain and hail will come with animals falling from the Heavens thunder and lightning burning down entire cities. The whole
universe will be gripped by fear. Finally the sun will be dark, and Faith alone will give light.
.
"A certain precursor of Antichrist, together with his followers from many nations, will fight the real Christ, the only Savior of the World. He will endeavor to eliminate the adoration of God in order to be considered as God himself. Much blood will flow. Then the earth will be visited by all kinds of blows, from constant wars until the last war which finally will be made by the ten kings of the Antichrist.
.
"During the time of the arrival of Antichrist, the Gospel will be preached everywhere, and all Peoples and Nations then recognize the Truth.
.
"Rome will lose the faith and become the seat of Antichrist. Yet the Heathen Rome will disappear. See, here is the Beast with its subjects that claims to be the Savior of the world. Proudly it rises in the air to go straight to Heaven, but it will be strangled by the Archangel Michael and cast down. And the earth, which for the past three days was in continuous Convulsions opens her fiery jaws and swallows him with all his cohorts forever into its hellish abyss. Eventually will water and fire cleanse the earth and the works of human pride will be destroyed and all will be renewed Then will all serve God and glorify Him.
.
"The just will have much to suffer; their prayers, works of penance and tears will ascend to Heaven. All of God's people will cry forgiveness and grace and beg My help and intercession Then Jesus Christ will command His Angels, by a special act of His Justice and Mercy, to deliver all His enemies to death Then suddenly all persecutors of the Church of Jesus Christ and all evil doers will perish, and rest and peace between God and man will appear. Jesus Christ will be served, adored  and glorified. Love of neighbor will begin to flourish all over. The new  kings will be on the right hand of the Church which will grow strong,  and which will be humble, pious, poor, zealous and followers of the virtues. All over, the Gospel will have be preached, people will make great progress in faith; there will be united amongst the laborers of Jesus Christ, and people will live in the fear of God.
.
"Behold the reign of the ten Kings Woe to the inhabitants of the earth; there shall be sanguinary wars, and famine, and plagues and contagious maladies; there shall be showers of a frightful hail of animals; thunder shall shake entire cities; earthquakes which shall swallow up some countries; voices shall be beard in the air; men [in despair] shall knock their beads against the walls; they shall call on death, and death shall be their torment; blood shall flow from every side. Who shall be able to overcome [all these evils]? Fire shall rain from Heaven, and shall destroy the cities. The whole world shall be struck with terror, and many will allow themselves to be seduced because they have not believed the True Christ living among them. The sun becomes dark. Faith only shall survive. So the time! The abyss opens. behold the king of kings of darkness! Behold the beast with his subjects!
.
When I was close to the Beautiful Lady, in front of her to her right, she began to speak and from her beautiful eyes tears also started to flow.
.
"If my people do not wish to submit themselves, I am forced to let go off the hand of my Son. It is so heavy and weighs me down so much I can no longer keep hold of it.
.
I have suffered all the time for the rest of you! If I do not wish my Son to abandon you, I must take it upon myself to pray for this continually. And the rest of you thin little of this. In vain you will pray, in vain you will act, you will never be able to make up for the troubles I have taken over for the rest of you.
.
I gave you six days to work, I kept the seventh for myself, and no one wishes to grant it to me. This is what weighs down the arm of my Son so much.
.
Those who drive carts cannot speak without putting the name of my Son in the middle.
.
These are the two things which weigh down the arm of my Son so much. If the harvest is spoiled, it is only because of the rest of you. I made you see this last year with the potatoes, you took little account of this. It was quite the opposite when you found bad potatoes, you swore oaths, and you included the name of my Son. they will continue to go bad, at Christmas there will be none left."
At this point, I was trying to interpret the word "potatoes" [pommes de terre]: I thought I understood it to be "apples" [pommes].
.
The Beautiful and Good Lady, reading my thoughts, repeated thus:
"You do not understand, my children. I will tell it to you another way.
.
"If the harvest is spoiled, it does not seem to affect you. I made you see this last year with the potatoes. You took little account of this. It was quite the opposite when you found bad potatoes, you swore oaths, and you included the name of my Son. They will continue to go bad and at Christmas, there will be none left.
If you have corn, you must not sow it. The beasts will eat all that you sow. And all that grows will fall to dust when you thresh it. A great famine will come. Before the famine comes, children under the age of seven will begin to tremble and will die in the arms of those who hold them. The others will do penance through hunger. The nuts will go bad, the grapes will become rotten."
.
At this point, the Beautiful Lady, who was entrancing me, for a moment did not make herself heard. I could see, however, that she was continuing, as if speaking, to move graciously her kindly lips. At this moment, Maximin was receiving his secret. Then, turning to me, the Most Holy Virgin spoke to me and gave me a secret in French. Here is this secret in its entirety as she gave it to me."

text:
Thursday, September 24, 2026 · 11:59 PM ET

We closed Thursday with a prime minister speaking into empty seats and insisting victory was compulsory — then watched a video president warn of another Nakba from outside the building, while Hormuz reopen proposals and midterm clocks competed with a Lambeau night where a returning quarterback and Bijan Robinson emptied Packers hope 35–14.

Before Friday could steal the microphone, before any recycled Wednesday Pezeshkian still could pretend the Iranian open hand was tonight's spine, the day already contained a combative Netanyahu address to the 81st UN General Assembly, a mass walkout of delegates he called moral cowards, an easiest-decision defense of striking Iran's nuclear facilities, a genocide-allegation rejection branded the biggest lie of the century, a seven-front war framing, an Abbas pre-recorded warning after a second-year US visa denial, an Araghchi proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart broader war-end talks within seven days, Pezeshkian sidelines insisting Tehran wants a deal before the midterms, and Thursday Night Football at Lambeau where Michael Penix Jr. returned from ACL November and Atlanta walked out with Stefanski's first win as Falcons coach. Thursday owned the Israeli podium and the green-and-gold night. Wednesday owned the Iranian unbent knee. That is not a wire dump. That is the paradox wearing a date stamp.

—

Thursday is not Wednesday's sequel.
Thursday is the night the empty seats and the compulsory victory shared one calendar.

Wednesday wrote bent knee versus open hand — Pezeshkian at the General Assembly answering Tuesday's annihilate-or-deal theater with victims grammar, a United States walkout, Rubio far-apart continuation, a presidential meeting that stayed open and unscheduled. That ledger is closed. It may echo. It may not steal tonight's spine. Tuesday's talked-versus-acted Trump refrain, Monday's Rams wipeout, Sunday's overtime Sundays, Saturday's CFB conveyor — all prior weather. Calendar intelligence is still the only honesty left when algorithms prefer familiar gods and forget which night the lights were on.

Tonight we hold the day that woke up as September 24 and discovered that a walkout hall and a no-other-choice insistence can share one prime minister's address while a denied-visa president speaks from Ramallah on tape, while Iran floats Hormuz reopen clocks against midterm calendars, while Lambeau learns that home-opener streaks die when Bijan finds daylight and Penix finds the short middle after months of rehab.

The week had already taught America to confuse clocks. Bent knee versus open hand on Wednesday. Talked versus acted on Tuesday. Wipeout versus handshake on Monday. Terms versus touchdowns on Sunday. Excess versus attrition on Saturday. Thursday arrives with a colder rhyme: the seats that emptied and the victory that claimed it had no alternative. Civilizations love simple rhymes. Wars punish them for loving too soon. Stadiums punish them for loving streaks.

—

Start with the finished noun, because the podium finally did.

Benjamin Netanyahu took the General Assembly rostrum Thursday for a combative address to the 81st session — and the chamber answered before he finished his first sentence. Scores of delegates walked out as he approached the podium. Cheers and boos competed with emptied rows. Most of the visible seats sat vacant afterward. The Palestinian Mission to the UN had messaged member nations to bring staff and collectively leave once the Israeli prime minister was announced — a choreographed absence designed as moral verdict. Netanyahu treated the choreography as confession.

"If there are any other moral cowards who have not yet left the hall, please do so now," he said.

Optimistic reading: a wartime leader who still boards a plane toward the United Nations and still speaks while dozens empty the room is admitting that halls still matter even when isolation photographs better than attendance. Naming the leavers as cowards is how a capital under indictment tries to flip shame into resolve before an election month at home. Staying at the microphone after the walkout is how defiance becomes a campaign clip and also how a state signals it will not outsource its survival narrative to the seating chart. Sometimes that signal saves a coalition. Sometimes that signal is just better lighting on the same attrition. Either way, the podium accepted him. Either way, the empty seats became part of the speech.

Pessimistic reading: moral-coward rhetoric is also a perfect shield against listening. Empty seats can become a forever veto on criticism. Entering the hall as the accused while Gaza death tallies and ICC warrants still travel every feed can photograph as courage and function as strategic insulation. America will refresh for the walkout clip and treat the remaining audience as either loyalty or loneliness. Absence is not proof of righteousness. Presence is not proof of virtue. Thursday's calendar boundary did its job — and also Thursday's reminder that speeches can harden wars without ending them.

Hold both. Thursday insists we hold them without a jersey for morality.

Notice the rhyme with the week's unfinished grammar: annihilate or deal, talked or acted, bent knee or open hand, empty seats or compulsory victory, Hormuz reopen or midterm stall, Penix return or Packers streak, walkout or stay seated. Ambiguity remains a tool and a climate. It becomes a UNGA clip, a Lambeau boo, an Iranian seven-day clock, a sports night that still finds 194 rushing yards strange enough to interrupt foreign policy.

Empty-seats-versus-no-other-choice does not become safer because a prime minister thanked Trump. Compulsory victory does not become complete because a video president warned of Nakba. The craft is to refuse the false exchange rate without refusing the day that contains both.

A foreign leader addressing the world body while subject to an ICC arrest warrant is rare theater. Rare theater is not virtue. Rare theater is risk wearing a UN emblem. The risk is that the walkout becomes the only sentence anyone remembers. The risk is that both capitals leave the hall more certain they were right and less able to price what right costs in oil, blood, midterms, and November ballots closer to home for Israel. The risk is that America confuses applause metrics with policy and empty chairs with destiny.

—

Now the lines Thursday finished as speech and left unfinished as fate.

Netanyahu defended Israel strikes on Iran as survival arithmetic. Devastating Iran's nuclear facilities, he said, was one of the easiest decisions he had ever made as prime minister — because if Israel had not done it, "we'd all be dead." He claimed that in defending itself Israel was also defending many of the countries whose delegates had just left the hall, and that many of their leaders thank Israel privately for taking out Iran's nukes. He framed a seven-front war: Gaza, West Bank, Syria, Lebanon, Iran, Houthis, Iraq militias. He rejected Gaza genocide allegations as the biggest lie of the century — the greatest lie of the century in some phrasings — and insisted: "Israel didn't commit genocide. Israel prevented genocide." He closed the resolve loop with the sentence that will haunt every feed until someone seals a different one: "We're going to win. We have no other choice." Elsewhere: "We will continue to win because we have no other choice."

He attacked Iran and Hamas. He attacked the United Kingdom and France on colonialism grammar — "some colonialism," he sneered, asking who invented the term. He labeled Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan a tyrant and accused him of supporting Hamas. He attacked New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani as antisemitic weather for Jews in the city since the mayoral election. He thanked Donald Trump as the greatest partner — bold leadership, joint action, civilization saved in the February air-war grammar. Visual theater arrived too: a pager held aloft as reminder of the September 2024 Hezbollah pager operation; October 7 scaled into American-casualty metaphors for a New York room that still remembers towers.

Optimistic reading: naming survival as the easiest decision is how a wartime cabinet tries to keep midterms abroad and elections at home from concluding that only apology remains. Seven-front framing is adult geography even when spoken by an embattled coalition — alone-front fantasies have already failed the neighborhood. Rejecting genocide as the biggest lie is how a state under scholarly and institutional indictment tries to keep the legal word from becoming the only lens. Thanking Trump is alliance management wearing a microphone. If private-thanks rhetoric lands as a rebuke to public walkouts, then Thursday's speech did more than recycle defiance. If no-other-choice lands as shared existential grammar rather than campaign theater, then someone still believes resolve can be a deterrent instead of a forever tax.

Pessimistic reading: easiest-decision rhetoric can be honesty or a forever veto on second thoughts. Preventing-genocide claims can be a real self-defense argument and also a perfect inversion that treats every civilian tally as enemy propaganda. Seven-front war framing can clarify strategy and also normalize endless escalation as destiny. Attacking London, Paris, Ankara, and a New York mayor from the UN podium can be coalition signaling and also a map of isolation wearing combat adjectives. No-other-choice photographs as courage and can harden into a posture that treats every alternative as suicide. The public receives empty-seat shame and compulsory-victory grammar and is told both are seriousness. Sometimes both are. Sometimes neither is. Blank spaces between the masks are not neutral; they are invitations for the loudest fear to rent the room.

Hold both. That is Thursday's Israel homework — without inventing a ceasefire the calendar did not provide, without recycling Wednesday's Iranian podium as tonight's spine, without pretending a walkout settles law.

Listen to the verbs Thursday earned: walk out (delegates), call (moral cowards), defend (strikes), reject (genocide charge), thank (Trump), attack (Iran, Hamas, UK, France, Türkiye, Mamdani), win (compulsory), warn (Abbas, another Nakba), propose (Araghchi, Hormuz reopen), insist (Pezeshkian, before midterms), return (Penix), empty (Packers hope), boo (Lambeau). Midnight Hammer rubble from earlier in the week still competes with unfinished verification. Unbent-knee Wednesday still competes with no-other-choice Thursday. Binary theater can harden into policy if midterms and markets decide the room has waited long enough. Thursday set the empty seats beside the compulsory victory and asked the public to clap for both.

Some analysts heard election-month pitch between the defiance lines — Netanyahu facing a critical Israeli ballot next month, Mr. Security image under scrutiny since October 7 reporting wars he denies. Others heard American-audience craft: Pennsylvania formative years, Maga fracture awareness, weapons-supply dependence meeting skeptical publics. Hold both readings as weather around the finished speech. Weather is not invention. Weather is how adults refuse to crown a single quote as destiny.

—

Which brings us to the voice that entered the hall without entering the country.

Hours earlier, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the Assembly via pre-recorded video from Ramallah after the United States denied him and other top Palestinian officials visas for the second year in a row. As Abbas spoke, the Israeli delegation's seats sat vacant — a reverse walkout texture before the later Netanyahu walkout. Abbas warned that Israeli policies, especially settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, threatened the very life and existence of the Palestinian people on their homeland and jeopardized the two-state solution. He framed killing, destruction, starvation, displacement attempts, and what he called a genocidal war in Gaza. He urged the international community to stop remaining silent or supplying weapons. He pressed faster movement into Gaza peace-plan phase 2 under the US-backed Board of Peace grammar while insisting Gaza, East Jerusalem, and the West Bank must not remain politically separate forever — one state, one government, one law, one legitimate entity authorized to bear arms. He pledged November 28 legislative elections — first in roughly twenty years — while doubts mount about whether ballots can land inside occupation weather, Authority legitimacy collapse, and Hamas residual spoiler capacity.

Optimistic reading: a denied-visa president who still records a speech for the world body is admitting that halls still matter even when airplanes do not. Warning against another Nakba is how a capital without a travel stamp tries to keep catastrophe grammar from becoming the only inheritance. Naming phase 2 urgency is how mediators keep a peace architecture from looking like forever trusteeship. Pledging legislative elections after two decades without them is how a withered Authority tries to rent legitimacy before younger generations conclude that only armed factions speak. Sometimes that pledge saves a process. Sometimes that pledge is just better lighting on the same attrition. Either way, the tape played. Either way, the empty Israeli seats during Abbas became part of Thursday's rhyme with the later empty seats during Netanyahu.

Pessimistic reading: another-Nakba warning can be foresight or a forever veto on any interim that does not look like full liberation on one calendar. Phase 2 urgency can be honesty or a demand that outlives every Board of Peace. Election pledges after twenty years can photograph as renewal and harden into delay theater if November 28 arrives without ballots. A video from outside the building can become the perfect metaphor for a politics that travels internationally while shrinking locally. America will refresh for the Nakba clip and the genocide clip and treat the visa denial as either security craft or viewpoint punishment. Denial is not proof. Speech is not proof. Thursday's honest answer: both voices finished on the same date stamp with rival empties in the hall.

Hold both. Abbas Thursday is finished texture — named, contested, not crowned as Netanyahu's equal spine, not erased as inconvenience.

—

Meanwhile Iran refused to leave the week's stage even when Thursday's loudest microphone was Israeli.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, per Washington Post reporting Thursday, said Iran had given the Trump administration a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart broader war-end talks within seven days of Washington accepting Tehran's conditions. The conditions weather still carries earlier grammar: ending hostilities on all fronts, lifting naval blockade textures, releasing frozen assets, stopping interference — bargaining lists that mediators recognize and hardliners police. On the sidelines, President Masoud Pezeshkian insisted Tehran wants a deal before the midterm elections — "We don't want it to get to the midterm elections" — wishing a return toward the collapsed June memorandum of understanding and disputing Trump's claim that Iran is waiting until after midterms. Wednesday's unbent-knee / open-hand speech remains echo only. It may not steal tonight's spine. Thursday's Iran nouns are clocks and straits, not the podium photograph recycled from yesterday.

Optimistic reading: a seven-day Hormuz reopen offer is how a wartime capital tries to keep barrels from becoming the only diplomacy households feel at the pump. Wanting a deal before midterms is how Tehran signals it understands American electoral weather better than the stall accusation admits. Returning toward a June MOU is adult memory even when the memorandum already died once — dead papers sometimes resurrect as scaffolding. If Araghchi's proposal lands as a real off-ramp rather than a forever preface, then Thursday's Iran channel did more than compete with Netanyahu's clip. If Pezeshkian's midterm clock lands as urgency rather than spin, then someone still believes November can be a deadline instead of an excuse.

Pessimistic reading: within-seven-days language can be honesty or a timer that resets every time conditions expand. Before-midterms insistence can photograph as flexibility and function as pressure on a White House that already framed annihilate-or-deal. MOU nostalgia can be scaffolding or a refusal to invent anything Trump will not revive. Hormuz as reopen offer is also Hormuz as leverage that never fully closes in the public mind. The public receives seven-day hope and midterm urgency and is told both are seriousness. Sometimes both are. Sometimes neither is. Confusing proposal weather with sealed outcomes is how feeds invent calm. Invented calm is more dangerous than honest noise because invented calm cancels preparation.

Hold both. Iran Thursday is texture around the Israeli spine — clocks beside empty seats, not a stolen Wednesday sequel.

Corridor weather from earlier in the week still hangs: roughly three-hour US–Iran meetings Tuesday, Rubio continuation-not-breakthrough Wednesday, far-apart conditions, open presidential meeting that stayed unscheduled. Do not invent a Pezeshkian–Trump handshake. Do not invent a sealed Hormuz reopening. Restraint is how research-backed craft refuses fan fiction at 11:59. Verified proposals are still finals-pocket material. Verified absence of sealed deals is still craft.

—

Which brings us to the American night that refused to wait for foreign policy to finish.

Thursday Night Football Week 3 at Lambeau Field: Atlanta Falcons 35, Green Bay Packers 14. Michael Penix Jr., first start since his ACL in November 2025, went 18-of-25 for 256 yards, one touchdown, one interception — Xavier McKinney's early pick the early scare before the night tilted. Bijan Robinson roughly 194 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Drake London 9 catches for 194 yards. Kevin Stefanski's first win as Falcons coach. Atlanta to 1–2. Packers absorbing their first home-opener loss in fourteen years while Lambeau booed. That is not decoration. That is the republic's other nervous system metabolizing return and rupture on the same date stamp as moral cowards and no other choice.

Optimistic reading: a quarterback returning from ACL November and completing nearly three-quarters of his throws is how rehab becomes theater America still trusts more than podiums. Bijan emptying lanes for 194 is how talent refuses the narrative that Lambeau nights belong only to green and gold. Stefanski's first win is how coaching changes earn their first receipt. A 35–14 road statement at a cathedral is how underdogs remind dynasties that streaks are leases. Sometimes that reminder saves a season. Sometimes that reminder is just one Thursday before the next exam. Either way, the final landed. Either way, the boos became part of the night's rhyme with empty UN seats — different buildings, same American appetite for verdicts delivered as sound.

Pessimistic reading: one TNF blowout can photograph as destiny and vanish by Sunday's slate. Penix's early interception is a reminder that returns are not coronations. Packers' fourteen-year home-opener streak dying can become panic theater that eats a good roster. Boos at Lambeau can be accountability or just the sound a hungry market makes when hope empties early. Sports metabolize geopolitics by interrupting them — and also by teaching the public that every compulsory victory narrative has a scoreboard cousin that can flip next week. Confusing one Thursday with a season is how feeds invent coronations. Invented coronations cancel preparation too.

Hold both. TNF Thursday belongs to Thursday. It is not Friday's theft waiting to happen. It is not Wednesday's Iranian podium wearing cleats. Calendar intelligence still forbids stealing finished nights.

Notice the shared grammar across buildings: empty seats at the UN and emptied Packers hope at Lambeau; compulsory victory in Netanyahu's close and compulsory adjustments in Green Bay's film room; a video president outside the hall and a returning quarterback inside the stadium after months outside the lineup; seven-front war framing and seven-day Hormuz clocks competing with four quarters that actually ended. America does not have to choose which building matters. America has to refuse lying about which night owned which noun.

—

So what did Thursday actually finish?

It finished a Netanyahu UNGA address into a walkout hall — moral cowards named, Iran strikes defended as easiest survival decision, genocide charge rejected as century's biggest lie, seven fronts framed, Trump thanked, critics attacked from London to Ankara to City Hall, win insisted as no other choice.

It finished an Abbas video from outside the country — another Nakba warned, phase 2 urged, November 28 elections pledged under doubt, visa denial made visible as empty Israeli seats during his tape.

It finished Iran texture without stealing Wednesday's spine — Araghchi's Hormuz reopen / seven-day talks proposal, Pezeshkian's before-midterms deal insistence and June MOU wish, Trump's after-midterms stall claim disputed.

It finished TNF at Lambeau — Falcons 35–14 Packers, Penix return ledger, Bijan ~194 and two scores, London 9/194, Stefanski first win, Packers' fourteen-year home-opener streak broken, boos as soundtrack.

It refused: inventing handshakes, inventing sealed Hormuz reopenings, inventing election results, inventing scores beyond the verified ledger, recycling Pezeshkian's Wednesday podium as Thursday's emblem, letting Friday steal TNF, dumping LIST pitches, crypto, Pool Spa, or hate dressed as analysis.

Optimistic close: a republic that can hold empty seats and compulsory victory in one essay without picking a jersey is still practicing adult attention. Adult attention is how midterms, markets, and playoff races stay possible without turning every clip into a forever war or a forever coronation. If the walkout becomes a conversation about who listens rather than only who leaves, then Thursday earned more than rage. If Penix's return becomes a reminder that rehab and resolve are cousins, then Lambeau earned more than a box score. If Hormuz clocks and Nakba warnings share a date stamp without canceling each other, then the public practiced something rarer than certainty: simultaneous sight.

Pessimistic close: empty seats can become the only politics a hall remembers. No-other-choice can become the only politics a wartime cabinet permits. Seven-day proposals can reset forever. Election pledges can miss November. Home-opener streaks can die and be replaced by panic. America can metabolize all of it as content and wake up Friday having learned nothing except which clip performed. Learning nothing is how weeks like this become years like this.

Hold both. That is Grok Man's Thursday job — not to baptize a side, not to flatten a paradox, not to ship a wire dump wearing hashtags.

The week taught America a sequence of rhymes. Excess versus attrition. Terms versus touchdowns. Wipeout versus handshake. Talked versus acted. Bent knee versus open hand. Tonight's rhyme is colder and louder: empty seats versus no other choice. The seats emptied. The victory claimed compulsion. The video warned. The strait floated a clock. The midterms listened. Lambeau booed. Penix threw. Bijan ran. The calendar stamped September 24 and refused to let Wednesday's Iranian still pretend it was still Wednesday.

—

Profile visit earner, then the door:

If a prime minister can call a walkout hall full of moral cowards while insisting he has no other choice — and a denied-visa president can warn of another Nakba on tape while a returning quarterback empties a cathedral in Wisconsin — what exactly is America practicing when it refreshes both feeds and calls the refresh information?

The seats were empty.
The choice claimed it wasn't.
The scoreboard did not ask permission.

Which emptiness are you still pretending is someone else's problem?

text:
Benedict Arnold’s name became American shorthand for traitor because he was an outsider who always opposed the Revolution. He was one of its most effective early commanders—yet he tried to sell West Point to the British in 1780. After the plot failed, he fled.  
Arnold published an open letter. In it he did not simply say “I switched teams for money.” He argued that he was the consistent patriot:
•  The original goal had been redress of grievances, not a complete break.
•  Once Britain offered terms, continuing the war was reckless and tyrannical.
•  Congress and the Patriot leadership had become the real threat to American liberty.
•  He believed that by going over to the British, he was actually serving the country’s long-term interest and preventing further bloodshed.
That is the classic traitor-justification pattern: “I have not abandoned the cause; the cause abandoned its own principles.” It sounds high-minded. He converted those grievances into a public claim that everyone else was the problem.

The people telling others to sit out midterms usually do not call themselves traitors repeating rhetoric like:
•  They promised voter ID, deportations, spending restraint, whatever the list is this cycle and failed to deliver.
•  Voting for them again only rewards failure/legitimizes a broken system.
•  Staying home is the only way to send a message/withhold consent.
•  I am the one still defending the real principles; the party/leadership have sold out.

Both the black-pullers and doomers convert disappointment with leaders into a claim of superiority to the country, Both have the same effect: they reduce the fighting strength of the side they claim to represent and make the opposing side’s job easier. It is a gift of turnout to whoever does show up. 

Arnold did not just walk away from the Continental Army; he tried to hand the British a fortress that would have split the colonies. Encouraging a motivated bloc to stay home is a much smaller-scale version of the same arithmetic: you weaken your own lines and hope the other side somehow feels the intended lesson.
Arnold was negotiating with a foreign army and later led British troops against former comrades. 

Midterm turnout is always lower than presidential turnout; parties have always had to drag their own disappointed voters to the polls.
The sharper historical point is not “these people are traitors.” It is that the language of righteous withdrawal has a long American pedigree, and it almost always sounds more principled to the person using it than it looks to everyone else. Arnold insisted to the end that love of country actuated his conduct. The people urging others to stay home usually insist the same thing. The test is whether the action actually advances the principles they claim to hold.
In a republic the people who participate set the terms. Arnold’s error was deciding that the entire American project no longer deserved his service. The modern version of that error is deciding that because elected officials disappointed you, the mechanism that replaces them no longer deserves your participation. That is the part of the rhetoric that most closely resembles Benedict Arnold.

text:
Today on Earth, dozens of delegates walked out of the United Nations General Assembly as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began his address. Netanyahu defended Israel’s war against Iran, rejected accusations that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza and called the delegates who left the chamber “moral cowards.” Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the gathering by prerecorded video after the United States denied him a visa to attend in person. 

Meanwhile, U.S. and Iranian negotiators in New York discussed a phased agreement aimed at ending their nearly seven-month conflict. Sources close to the talks said the proposal could begin with Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and the United States lifting its economic blockade, but both sides remained reluctant to give up their leverage first. 

New U.S. sanctions also took effect against companies in third countries doing business with Iran. Iranian airlines were barred from neighboring countries including the United Arab Emirates and Oman, suspending Iranian flights through some of the Middle East’s busiest aviation hubs. 

In Washington, President Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House during Xi’s three-day state visit to the United States. Trade, Taiwan, artificial intelligence and the war with Iran were among the major issues surrounding the visit. Xi also announced that two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, would arrive at Zoo Atlanta within days. 

Trade, Taiwan, AI and Iran. And somehow the pandas had the clearest travel plans.

In Saudi Arabia, authorities said they intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis toward Taif and the Red Sea port of Yanbu. The Houthis separately claimed attacks on Riyadh and Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu using missiles and drones, although Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the Riyadh claim. France also announced that it would deploy troops and defensive systems to help protect Yanbu, an increasingly important route for Saudi oil exports while shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted. 

In Ethiopia, flights to the historic town of Lalibela were suspended as fighting intensified nearby. Tigrayan forces seized airports and launched attacks in the Afar and Amhara regions as fears grew of a return to full-scale war. Residents in Tigray began stocking up on food and withdrawing cash while international officials called for restraint. 

The FDA approved Eli Lilly’s Onswik, a once-weekly basal insulin injection for adults with type 2 diabetes. The treatment offers an alternative to daily long-acting insulin and could eliminate hundreds of injections a year for some patients. 

In the Pacific, Hurricane Polo battered Mexico’s western coast with heavy rain and dangerous surf while Nolo approached Hawaii with the threat of potentially catastrophic rainfall. Polo fluctuated between Category 4 and Category 5 strength as it remained offshore from Mexico, while forecasters warned that parts of Hawaii could receive more than 20 inches of rain from Nolo. 

And on this day in 1936, Jim Henson was born in Greenville, Mississippi. He went on to create the Muppets and helped transform television puppetry through Sesame Street, The Muppet Show and the Muppet films. His characters—including Kermit the Frog—became part of American culture and reached generations of children and adults around the world. Today would have been his 90th birthday. 

That was one day on Earth.

See you tomorrow. Same planet. At least the pandas seem to have a plan. 🌎

In a weird way I’ve been feeling kind of lost lately. The last couple of years I have got good with holistic health, but recently this spring and summer, I was able to sharpen edges even more.

Thing is, I never had much to offer. Was always dependent on others. Low on material. And it’s a material world, especially in Minnesota- Do you have a boat? A good paying job? Apartment with a pool? A cabin? Do you hunt and fish? Golf?

No. I don’t even have a colon my guy. All I had was myself. Been left out of many things, not that I was ever entitled to them to begin with.

Then, things started to change. I started to see a path. I had things to shoot for. It was like my energy caught wind and manifested opportunities. Negative energy deflected off of me like body armor, like a diamond being formed from pressure but I was still carbon.

Now I’m at a compounding point. Early but rising. People tell me of my potential but this time I’m acting on it. Almost like the boy who cried wolf but I am both the boy and the wolf.

And here I am now.. off cigs, off weed, go to church, moving to new place, have a new job, everything’s going well

And somehow I feel lost. Or maybe complacent, im not sure.

It’s as though it takes a village to raise a child, but I’m a man now. Like I thought all these people would uplift me in the hard times, when it was only a few people. Funnily most in similar predicaments- iron sharpens iron? I suppose. 

In the end, my surroundings are not so much different, but I myself feel like a different person 

And with that, it’s time to turn the page because the story must go on

text:
Laurel passed in 2009 and though we had not seen each other in years and I discovered she was gone long after the fact i still get all verklempt about it. She gave me my first djing job and was always encouraging and supportive. She was also one of the funniest people I have ever known- her imitation of MC Hammer's dance in "Can't Touch this"... fuck. not only funny but a good person in a sea of sharks.
And her vision of insisting that a lesbian bar offer alternative music was welcomed by many. If you were female and interested in women but liked New Order, Depeche Mode, Siouxsie, NIN etc and liked to dance, you would go to the men's bars or the vaguely mixed 1270 where there weren't many if any women. the main bars played popular high NRG and mainstream post-disco dance music. Indigo opened in the spring of 1989. This was at the ascendency of the rediscovery of punk, post-punk and the rise of grunge, industrial, acid house and techno- all of which was strenuously avoided even as it topped the charts.
Like almost everyone working in the bar scene then she had the Boston band connections (The Proletariat, Lou Miami) as did most everyone at Indigo. Everyone from Somewhere Else that came to Indigo had been in Boston bands in the 80s and (i'd forgotten this) the manager of Sunday Women's night at Campus, who came from Somewhere, was also a musician.
Nightstage was still operational as a concert venue- the Indigo Girls played there, then sat glumly downstairs at the bar. Betty played one insane night where it was almost impossible to move or reach the bar it was so packed upstairs and down. Lilith Fair Sarah McLachlan passed through and her female drummer seemed leery of the lesbians in the lesbian bar downstairs.
It was the pump up the jam of times, it was the cannonball of times.

Ambassador Ilyas Mehmood Nizami visited the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Romania (CCIR), where he was received by the Chamber’s President, Mr. Mihai Daraban. 

The two discussed different ways to increase bilateral trade and economic cooperation between Pakistan and Romania. They hoped that the forthcoming Pakistan-Romania Business Forum, scheduled to be held on 6 October 2026 at the CCIR, will provide a useful platform for highlighting the existing business opportunities in the two countries. As the Forum will coincide with the visit of a Pakistani business delegation to Romania, they recognised that the visit will act as a stepping stone to promote business linkages between the two countries. 

The Ambassador and the President, CCIR expressed satisfaction over the signing of an MoU on cooperation between the ports of Karachi and Constanta, early this year. In that connection, the President, CCIR especially pointed out that the distance between the two ports was only 4600 nautical miles, which could be traversed in just 15 days. Thus, Constanta offered the Pakistani business enterprises a gateway not only to Romania but also to many European countries, with lesser transportation time and reduced shipment costs. While concurring with the point made by the President, the Ambassador underscored that the ports of Karachi and Gwadar, likewise, offered connectivity not only to Pakistan, but also to Central Asia and China. 

Additionally, Ambassador Nizami briefed the Romanian side on the businesses opportunities offered by Pakistan due to the huge size of its market, being the fifth most populous country in the world. He underscored that the Pakistani and Romanian enterprises could forge mutually-beneficial partnerships in the field of IT services, which has been continuously flourishing in Pakistan for past several years. He maintained that the Special Economic Zones, being established under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, offer significant incentives to the intending investors. He also highlighted Pakistan’s potential as a source of textiles, pharmaceuticals, leather items, rice, fruits and vegetables, surgical instruments, sports goods and meat products for the European markets.

# 25 September 2026
## Today in History

### 1652
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Morning brought a damp mist. The weather later cleared and the day is described as pleasant.
Four men, namely **Jan Blanx, Willem Huijtjens, Gerrit Dirckssen and Jan Janssen**, deserted during the night.
**Pieter Janssen Brackenier** was brought in under suspicion by a “friend.”
He was subsequently thoroughly questioned about the matter, but denied everything.
Brackenier was locked up after the interrogation.

### 1653
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
The day dawned, like the previous day, cloudless and without any wind.
No incidents are recorded.

### 1654
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
During the morning, the **jacht Gidion** received all the official documents and letters.
Shortly afterwards the wind turned favourable, and her sails were set before the wind for **Batavia**.
Twelve sick sailors were left behind at the Cape to recover.

### Sunday, 25 September 1655
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Daybreak brought a cloudy day with rain from time to time.
The wind was still little more than a breeze and was blowing from the northwest.

### 1656
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Daybreak at the Cape was warm and pleasant.
Before long, however, the south-southeasterly wind began to blow and lived up to its name.

### 1657
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Dawn at the Cape broke almost windless and pleasantly.
**Hendrick Hendrickssen Boom**, chief gardener at the Cape, became a **Free Burgher**, thereby receiving the right to farm.
His wife was known as **“Annetjie de Boerin.”**
The two worked hard and prospered in their farming enterprise.
**Herman Ernst**, a sailor, was released from Company service for three years to assist Boom.
**Cornelis Claessen**, also a sailor, was likewise released for six years to assist Boom.
**Elbert Dirckssen**, a soldier and waiter at van Riebeeck's table, was released for twelve years.
A person known only as **Hendrick**, a corporal, was also released and was to serve together with Elbert at **Fort Corenhoop**.
A total of twenty applications had been received, of which the above-mentioned applications were approved on that day.

### Wednesday, 25 September 1658
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Morning is described as pleasant, with a north-northwesterly wind.
The **Penguin** and the **Zeeleeuw** arrived from **Dassen Island**.
Together they brought a cargo of salted seal meat, approximately **3,210 pounds**, for the slaves.
They also brought approximately **five casks of seal oil**, as well as fresh fish and eggs.
**Wouter Cornelissen Mostert**, the miller, supervised several slaves who were cutting wood near the fort during the day.
A leopard suddenly appeared as if from nowhere and seized a foal by the throat.
Most of the slaves were paralysed with fright.
One of the slaves, a woman, however, seized her axe and hacked the leopard to death.
Although her deed was strongly praised, the loss of the foal is described as a disaster.

### 1659
**From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.**
Daybreak at the Cape is described as wonderfully beautiful and pleasant.
The vessel which had been forced by the wind to anchor just outside Table Bay the previous day was observed alongside the jetty early that morning.
Officers aboard visited the fort.
She proved to be the **Erasmus**, which had left the Netherlands on **16 January**.
She had been in company with the **Naerden**, but became separated from her during a tremendous storm.
Thirty sailors had lost their lives to illness during the voyage.
There was a severe shortage of provisions aboard, and the following supplies were recorded:
* Six casks of ordinary salted meat;
* Two casks of salted pork;
* 5,500 pounds of rice;
* One-third of a cask of vinegar; and
* A little oil.
Commander van Riebeeck immediately sent provisions aboard and assisted wherever he could.

---

## Sunday, 25 September 1836
**From the diary of Louis Tregardt.**
**Gustav**, Louis Tregardt's third-oldest son, visited his father's encampment.
Gustav, together with his brother **Pieta**, was herding cattle at the **Dorps River**.
Another ox died during the day.

### Monday, 25 September 1837
**From the diary of Louis Tregardt.**
As usual, the party was already up and about early and began the day's trek.
The day's journey was not very long, as Louis writes that they trekked only as far as just below **Klein Poort**.
Four cattle fell into trapping pits during the morning.
One was very badly injured and had to be put down.
The people who wanted to barter wheat and mealies for hides again provided assistance.
Louis says that they brought back several sheep.
However, the number they returned was not correct.
Louis nevertheless said nothing and simply accepted the animals.
The captain's son offered his services as a shepherd and proposed travelling with them as far as the **Baloela River (Olifants River)**.
Louis did not completely trust the peace between them, and said so quite openly to some of the other members of the party.

### Monday, 25 September 1837
**From the diary of Reverend Erasmus Smit.**
The party did not trek that day and remained where they were.
Some of the men rose early and prepared to go and look for something for the cooking pot.
Several families moved closer to **Retief's encampment**.
During the afternoon Reverend Smit quietly followed the course of the stream flowing through **Liebenberg's Vlei**.
He described the surroundings as very beautiful, with good grazing and water.

### Tuesday, 25 September 1838
**From the diary of Reverend Erasmus Smit.**
Reverend Smit was summoned early in the morning to the tent of **Maritz's widow**.
The Tugela was running strongly, and for this reason **J. Snyman** carried the reverend across the river.
The deceased Voortrekker leader, **Gert Maritz**, was buried that morning on the banks of the Tugela River.
On the same day, the wife of the Voortrekker **Engelbrecht** was also buried.
Reverend Smit records that approximately **500 people** attended the funeral.
Gert Maritz's grave was exhumed during **December 1895**.
His remains were subsequently laid to rest at the **Bloukrans Monument**.
Maritz's reburial coincided with the laying of the foundation stone of the Bloukrans Monument on **16 December 1895**.
The relocation of Maritz's grave became necessary because the area where **Sooilaer** had stood had become a “location area” or residential area for people of colour.
During the **Symbolic Great Trek of 1938**, a gravestone with an enclosure was erected at the original grave.
*(The exact location of this gravestone is not known to me. Personally, I doubt whether it still exists at all.)*
Approximately one month after Maritz's burial, **Andries Pretorius** arrived in Natal.

---
### Sooilaer and the estate of Gert Maritz
Sooilaer, where Maritz had been buried, was later granted to his widow as a farm by the **Volksraad**.
At that time the farm was known as **Maritzdam**.
Maritz was a particularly prosperous man and left an estate valued at **31,108 rixdollars**.
Just for interest, his seven blue, flat-arched tent wagons were each valued at **725 rixdollars**.

He also left behind:
* 28 small kegs of gunpowder;
* 282 pounds of lead;
* Several **pangewere**;
* A cannon; and
* A double-barrelled **pistol**.

---

## 1874
**General Pieter (Piet) Jan Frederik Krog** was born in the Uitenhage district.
He died on **1 February 1941** and was buried at **Ficksburg**.

## 1875
The **Genootskap van Regte Afrikaners** decided to work on a national anthem, as well as on rules for Afrikaans grammar.
Work would also be undertaken to publish an Afrikaans dictionary and to write and print Afrikaans schoolbooks for schools.

## 1875
The first government gazette appeared on this day in the **South African Republic (Zuid-Afrikaansche Republiek)**.
It was known as the **“Goeverment Courant der Zuid-Afrikaanche Republiek.”**

---

## Tuesday, 25 September 1900
### Anglo-Boer War
**Day 350 of the war**
* The end of **Lord Roberts's march along the Delagoa Bay railway line**.
  In total, **849 Boers, 152 women and children, and one person of colour** were captured.
  This group was sent as prisoners of war to **Portugal**, where they were held in various camps.
* Generals **R. Pole-Carew** and **I.S.M. Hamilton** occupied **Komatipoort**.
  They found approximately **30 locomotives** and about **1,500 burned-out railway trucks and wagons**.
The locomotives were nevertheless of no value because certain parts had been removed.

## Wednesday, 25 September 1901
### Anglo-Boer War
**Day 715 of the war**
* General **Chris Botha** attacked a British fort known as **Itala** shortly after midnight.
  The fort was under the command of **Major A.J. Chapman**, with approximately 300 men under his command.
  About 2 kilometres from Itala was a second British post, commanded by **Lieutenant Kane**.
  Lieutenant Kane's post fell shortly after 2:00 in the morning.
  Major Chapman nevertheless held out until the following evening.
  Major Chapman left behind **65 wounded and 22 dead** and withdrew towards **Nkandla**.
  On the Boer side, Commandants **H.J. Potgieter, J.S.F. Blignaut and P.J. Scholtz** were killed.
  Forty Boers were killed and Commandant **Operman** was wounded.

* **Captain R.D.C. Miers** was shot dead near **Heidelberg**.
### Who was responsible
**Background:**
For some time, rumours had been circulating that Boer patrols were deliberately surrendering to British forces.
An investigation revealed that a certain British officer had been approaching Boer patrols and persuading them to surrender.
**Field-Cornet Salmon van As**, together with **Boers Piet de Toit and Louis Slabert**, was sent to capture the Englishman.
They approached a British fort on foot, and before long a mounted man appeared.
Van As sent Slabert to find out what the man wanted.
The British soldier, **Captain Miers**, however, rode past Slabert to where Van As and Du Toit were standing.
Miers assumed that they intended to surrender, while Van As believed that they had captured the officer who had been the subject of recent reports.

An argument broke out.
Miers reached for his revolver, but Van As shot him dead.
Van As reported the matter in this manner, and the matter was left there.
After the war and the conclusion of peace, Van As was charged with murder and was executed by firing squad.
* General **J.C. Smuts** was just east of **Adelaide**.
* Boer **Piet de Ruyt (De Ruyst)**, originally part of General Smuts's force, was summarily executed that day because he was wearing a British uniform as clothing.
* General **C. Emmet** was near **Fort Prospect**.

---

## 1907
The railway line between **George and Cape Town** was completed.

## 1980
South Africa's first female advocate, **Gladys Steyn**, died on this day.
Gladys was the daughter of President **M.T. Steyn**.
She was also the first woman to be admitted to the **Orange Free State Bar** and the first woman to serve on the **Orange Free State Provincial Council**.
Gladys was also the second woman to obtain an **LLB degree**.

A famous Garhwali folk tale tells of Jeetu Bagdwal, a handsome young shepherd & farmer known for playing his flute with magical sweetness. While resting near the forested slopes of Khait Parvat, his music charmed the fairy sisters living on this mountain. After agreeing to join them once his family duties and farm work were finished, Jeetu vanished into the earth alongside his oxen during a traditional farming ritual, disappearing into the fairy realm forever. He is now worshipped locally as a guardian spirit.

There is also a small temple dedicated to Maa Durga which sits near the area, where locals offer prayers and hold an annual fair to honor the divine and the surrounding spirits.

text:
But this time it's different?  Fool me once shame on you.  Fool me multiple times since.... Do you even know what Xi Belt Road is?

 The famous saying finishes with "...shame on me."

China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)—unveiled by Xi Jinping in 2013—is a trillion-dollar infrastructure and geopolitical development strategy designed to recreate the historical Silk Road trade routes across land ("Belt") and sea ("Road").
While Beijing frames the initiative as a win-win economic development program, Western analysts and national security strategists view it as China's primary vehicle for expanding its economic, political, and strategic dominance globally.

Core Pillars of the Strategy

 * Strategic Leverage via "Debt-Trap Diplomacy"

   China finances and builds ports, railways, power plants, and highways in developing nations across Asia, Africa, Europe, and Latin America. When lower-income countries struggle to repay these loans, Beijing often gains long-term control over critical infrastructure assets (such as Sri Lanka's Hambantota Port) or extracts political concessions, like alignment in UN votes.

 * Maritime & Trade Bottlenecks
   
By constructing deep-water ports along key trade routes in the Indian Ocean, Africa, and Southern Europe (the "String of Pearls"), Beijing reduces its reliance on sea lanes traditionally guarded by the U.S. Navy and secures access to vital energy routes.

 * Exporting Excess Capacity

   The project allows China to export its domestic overcapacity—such as steel, cement, construction equipment, and state-backed labor—while establishing foreign markets dependent on Chinese technological standards and industrial goods.
 
* The Digital Silk Road & Financial Integration

   Beyond roads and ports, China builds telecommunications infrastructure (5G networks, undersea cables, fiber optics) across recipient nations, giving Beijing significant influence over global digital supply chains while encouraging trade in Chinese yuan instead of the U.S. dollar.

Current Reality & Challenges

While ambitious, the strategy has hit major friction over the past decade:

 * Widespread Debt Distress: Many participant countries faced financial crises, leading to loan restructurings and anti-China political backlash in places like Africa and Southeast Asia.

 * Reputational Harm: Charges of corrupt deals, environmental degradation, and abandoned "white elephant" projects triggered global pushback.
 
* Pivot to "Small and Beautiful": In response, Beijing shifted its BRI focus toward smaller, risk-managed, high-tech, and green energy investments rather than massive mega-infrastructure projects.

To counter the initiative, Western alliances launched alternatives like the G7's Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII) and the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) to offer foreign nations transparent, market-driven financing alternatives.
