Los Angeles, California | September 22, 2026

The camera was covering freeway traffic. Then a strange object became the story.

According to The California Post, a FOX 11 news helicopter captured a spherical object above a busy Los Angeles freeway interchange during Tuesday’s live traffic coverage. The camera reframed its shot to follow the object, and clips spread across social media.

The footage prompted competing explanations: a balloon, a drone, or something else. Some viewers argued that its apparently straight movement ruled out a balloon—but a straight-looking path alone cannot establish what an object is. Wind, camera movement, and perspective all need consideration.

What makes this case interesting is the reported source: a routine news broadcast with traffic below providing visual context. However, a recognizable source does not automatically establish the object’s size, distance, speed, or identity.

The September 24 article offered no confirmed identification. Claims connecting the object to extraterrestrials—or to separate sightings in Iran—remain unsupported by the supplied report.

A routine object from an unusual angle, or something that deserves a closer look? What do you see?

text:
"I had nothing to contribute really is what I thought."

The next auction of American airwaves is being prepared right now. Nobody is redesigning the mechanism, because it was solved thirty years ago.

He says it about the moment he was asked to help design the sale of a country's radio spectrum. He was a theorist. He had, in his words, no practical experience.

Paul Milgrom is telling this in his Nobel lecture, and the design he and Bob Wilson produced in 1993 has since been used to sell, by his count, hundreds of billions of dollars of licences around the world.

The idea came from a charity dinner. At a silent auction, many items sit on tables at once, each with a bid sheet, and people walk around comparing. That was exactly what a telephone company needed: it wanted licences covering Northern and Southern California and had to work out which ones were cheapest before committing.

The theory came later. The first move was noticing that a room full of wine bottles and bid sheets solved a problem the government's proposed format did not.

Where the design actually came from:

> A familiar format, watched closely for what goes wrong in it.
> One flaw named precisely: last-minute bidding.
> Two rules written to remove that flaw.
> Theory used to check the fix, not to invent it.

If you are someone who assumes the expert in the room started with a model, this is five minutes that will annoy you pleasantly.

Nine thousand people, over five years, have heard him admit how little he thought he had to offer.

Save this before you scroll on. The list in the middle is the whole point.

The man who thought he had nothing to contribute designed the format for the largest asset sales the American government runs. What would your version of a charity auction be?

Iran War Update, Month 7 (Sept 25)

The US naval blockade is squeezing Tehran, and Iran is feeling it. At the UN this week, Iran's leaders said they want a deal before the US midterms. Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran gave US mediators a 7-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart peace talks. President Pezeshkian said Iran is "open" to nuclear inspections. But Iran is still demanding that Washington move first. Its security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, says Hormuz stays closed and there will be no negotiations until Iran's seven conditions are met, starting with lifting the blockade. Sources told The National that Iran offered no concessions in New York.

Washington is right not to fall for it. Secretary Rubio says there has been no breakthrough, and the blockade stays. America's allies agree. The Wall Street Journal reports that Saudi Arabia and the UAE are urging Washington to keep the blockade and sanctions in place until Iran signs a new agreement. About 80 countries backed a joint UN statement demanding Hormuz reopen and condemning Iran's attacks on shipping and on its neighbors. The US and Europe are drafting a Security Council plan for an international naval mission to protect shipping in the strait. At home, the Senate narrowly rejected a resolution to limit the President's war powers.

The threats are still real. An Iranian adviser warned that Iran and the Houthis could open a "new front" against Red Sea energy supplies. The Houthis have seized Yemen's Mokha coast and attacked Saudi oil facilities at Yanbu, and France is sending forces to help protect that terminal. A commercial ship was hit in Hormuz on Wednesday, killing one sailor. Brent crude is above $105.

At the UN, Netanyahu thanked President Trump and said the allies "crushed" Iran's army, navy, air force and nuclear sites. Mediators hope to hold talks in Oman as early as next week. The message from Washington should stay simple: reopen the strait, let inspectors in, then we talk. Holding firm is what brought Iran to the table.

UConn played football in the American from 2014 to 2019 before going independent for the second time in its history.

text:
I started dreading bedtime.

That’s when you realize a noise problem has gone beyond being annoying.

When you’re lying in bed wondering, “How many times am I going to wake up tonight?”

I began listening for the baby before I even fell asleep.

Then came the first scream.

I’d look at the clock.

11:43 PM.

I’d finally fall asleep again.

Another scream.

2:17 AM.

Then another.

4:06 AM.

The next morning, I’d be exhausted before my day had even started.

And yet I felt guilty for being angry.

Because these were children.

I knew babies cried.

I knew parents got tired.

I knew toddlers weren’t exactly famous for their ability to move quietly.

I wasn’t asking for perfection.

I was asking for some awareness.

Some acknowledgment.

Maybe even a simple, “We’re sorry, we’re doing our best.”

Instead, every conversation made us feel like we were imagining the problem.

That’s what bothered me more than the noise.

I could tolerate a crying baby.

I could tolerate occasional stomping.

I could tolerate the occasional slammed door.

What I couldn’t tolerate was feeling completely dismissed.

At this point, I’ve seriously considered moving.

Not because I hate the family.

Not because I think children shouldn’t live in apartments.

But because I miss sleeping without being startled awake.

I miss sitting in my own home without feeling vibrations beneath my feet.

I miss not knowing what time the neighbors’ children are awake.

And honestly?

I’m starting to understand why people pay ridiculous amounts of money for detached houses.

If someone offered me one million euros right now with the condition that I spend the rest of my life in a tiny house in the middle of nowhere, I’d sign the paperwork before they finished the sentence.

No upstairs neighbor.

No downstairs neighbor.

No shared hallway.

No slamming doors.

No stomping.

No midnight screaming through the ceiling.

Just me, my boyfriend, a quiet house, and absolutely nobody living underneath us.

Until then, I guess I’ll keep reminding myself that apartment living comes with noise.

But there’s a difference between hearing your neighbors…

and feeling like you’ve accidentally moved into their living room.

text:
OSV News posted a real Élysée dispatch. On 25 September at the palace in Paris, the account said Pope Leo XIV praised France’s service of the common good, pointed to the restoration of Notre-Dame as proof that “what seemed irreparably destroyed can be reborn through mutual cooperation” and as “an eloquent witness to the unity born of commitment to a common cause,” warned that science and technology unguided by wisdom can “offer immediate solutions that apparently address people's wishes and their pain, but can seriously divert them from the greater good to which they aspire,” named “genetic manipulation, surrogacy, the trade in human organs or the possibility of arranging one's own death,” insisted that “the protection of every human life is a duty incumbent upon each and every one of us,” and closed by urging France to be “a tireless champion of peace and multilateralism” and to help build “a peace that is unarmed and disarming.” A pool photograph is attached. Those are the words.

What holds: The Holy Father did address the President, the authorities, civil society, and the diplomatic corps at the Élysée on the first morning of the France journey. He did thank the President for the Notre-Dame works. He did set the rebuilt cathedral against despair. He did warn against a “paradise of machines.” He did list those four practices in one sentence. He did call the protection of every human life a duty of each person. He did ask France to remain a champion of peace and multilateralism and to work for a peace that is unarmed and disarming. The hard list is in the tweet. An official Catholic news service can put the life paragraph in the same post as the compliment to France.

What fails: The tweet is a polished digest. The official text says “something considered irreparably destroyed” and that the restoration “bore eloquent witness.” OSV turns both into cleaner marble. The same paragraph the account quotes about arranging one’s own death begins with “profit-driven ventures.” That clause is gone. So is the line that immediately precedes the list: that “the protection of the right to life constitutes the indispensable foundation of every other human right.” Readers who have not followed the Assemblée since July do not learn that France created a legal path to assisted dying in August, that no procedure has yet been carried out, and that the Pope spoke those words in the palace where the law was signed without naming the statute. They also do not get the French argument he then made: that authentic laïcité does not exile a Christian conscience from public service. Magnifica Humanitas, Bernanos, Clovis, the Universal Declaration, and the Pope’s own roots in Normandy and Béarn stay in the hall. A service that exists to say what is happening in the Church and why it matters can keep the foundation-of-rights sentence beside the four practices, and can say in which country, in which month, the fourth one became law.

Accurate list, softened frame, nearly full tweet. OSV did not invent Notre-Dame or the duty to life. It announced the restored cathedral and the unarmed peace and left the new French statute, laïcité, and the foundation of every other right in the speech.

Grade: B+

text:
Or they are scared of AI audits ..

Yes — this is one of the better uses of AI and automated audits, because favoritism in land sales and contracts usually leaves a paper trail across public databases that humans only sample once a year.
What it would actually catch faster:
•City/county real estate sales below market. Memphis surplus land is supposed to be valued and, above $20,000, go through Council. Shelby County Land Bank tax-sale properties are advertised and open to competing offers. AI can flag sales far below assessor value or recent comps, repeat buyers, and LLCs that keep winning cheap parcels.
•Same people on both sides. Cross-matching deeds, Secretary of State LLC filings, vendor lists, campaign reports, and employee/relative addresses can show a council member’s family LLC buying city lots or a department head’s relative winning contracts.
•Sweetheart contract terms. Unusual no-bid awards, bid splitting under the threshold, one vendor winning far more than peers, change orders that inflate price after award, or a contractor’s staff sitting in on hiring that later controls their own contracts — the recent MSCS forensic audit found exactly those patterns the old way, after the money was spent.
•Local-preference loopholes. Shelby County’s locally owned small-business program has been used so a certified firm wins, then subcontracts the real work. Pattern detection spots that quickly.
What it would not prove by itself: that someone is a “friend” or that a cheap blight sale was corrupt rather than a legal redevelopment deal. That still needs human review, interviews, and sometimes subpoenas.
The bottleneck is the same as before: the city and county have to feed deeds, bid tabs, contracts, change orders, and vendor ownership into one place. Those records already exist electronically in pieces (Register of Deeds, Land Bank notices, Council packets, purchasing files). Linking them and running continuous related-party and under-market checks would flag friends-and-family deals months sooner than waiting for the next annual audit or a whistleblower.

text:
On September 25, 1981, a ranch-raised lawyer from Arizona placed her hand on a Bible, raised the other, and became the first woman ever to sit on the United States Supreme Court. In that quiet courtroom, America did more than fill a vacancy. It proved, again, that this country still belongs to people willing to work, endure, and rise.

Sandra Day O’Connor did not inherit the bench. She earned it the hard American way.

She grew up on the Lazy B, a remote cattle ranch on the Arizona–New Mexico line. Water was scarce. Work was not. She branded cattle, drove trucks, and held her own among ranch hands who had not asked for a girl in their crew. 

That life taught her something no classroom can fully give: competence first, complaint later. “It had been an all-male domain,” she later wrote. Changing it was her first initiation into rooms that were not built for her.

She entered Stanford at 16, finished law school near the top of her class, and then discovered what many gifted women of her generation discovered: the door could still slam. 

Law firms that would not hire her as a lawyer offered her work as a secretary. She did not wait for permission. She built a practice. She served as an assistant attorney general. She entered the Arizona Senate and became the first woman in the country to serve as majority leader of a state senate. Then she became a trial judge, then an appellate judge. 

When President Reagan kept his campaign promise and nominated her in 1981, the Senate confirmed her 99–0. Four days later, on this date, she was sworn in. 

That is the American pattern at its best: talent plus grit, then a nation large enough to recognize both.

O’Connor understood the weight of being first. 

She later said she did not want to be the last woman on the Court. If she did a poor job, she feared it would be a long time before another woman was trusted with the same responsibility. 

So she did the job. 

She read the briefs. 

She asked hard questions. 

She wrote careful opinions. 

She did not ask the country to applaud her gender. She asked it to judge her work. “The power I exert on the Court depends on the power of my arguments, not on my gender,” she said. That is not a small sentence. It is a standard. 

Women who want high goals should take that standard seriously.

High office is not a mood. It is a craft. O’Connor’s path was not a slogan about “smashing ceilings.” It was years of unglamorous competence: statutes read line by line, cases decided when the law and her feelings were not the same thing, a reputation built where people could see the work. She once advised that the first step toward power, for men and women alike, is to become visible—and then to put on an impressive show. As women achieve, she said, barriers fall, because society sees what women can do and women see it too. 

That is patriotic advice. 

The American promise has never been that life will be easy. It has been that effort can still change a life, and that a republic is stronger when it uses all of its talent. A nation that tells half its people to shrink is a nation leaving power on the table. A nation that demands excellence from everyone, then opens the door to those who meet the demand, is a nation keeping faith with itself.

So the lesson of September 25 is not that history hands out firsts. It is that firsts are usually the last chapter of a long apprenticeship.

Do the work in the room you are in. Master the unfashionable details. Take the job nobody wanted if it teaches you how institutions actually run. Serve your community before you demand that the country serve you. Learn to hold your own in hard company. When the door opens, walk through it ready—not as a symbol, but as someone who can carry the load.

text:
THE WEIRDEST EVENTS IN HISTORY: STRANGER THAN FICTION, 100% REAL.  🤯

SEPTEMBER 25th EDITION

“Truth is stranger than fiction, but it is because Fiction is obliged to stick to possibilities; Truth isn't.” ~ Mark Twain

September 25th isn’t the day history puts on its tailored suit and gives a heroic speech; it’s the day history stumbles home at 3:00 AM, trips over its own shoelaces, and desperately tries to pretend nobody saw.

275 AD — The Senate Finally Picked an Emperor—Then Never Did It Again.  👑

The Roman Senate elects an emperor for the last time in its long history, choosing 75-year-old Marcus Claudius Tacitus. After centuries of generals, barracks emperors, and raw military power deciding who wore the purple, the old assembly briefly reclaimed the role—then never did it again.

🧩 Trivia: Tacitus lasted only about six months before dying on campaign, and the Senate’s brief revival of authority vanished almost as quickly as it appeared.

1066 — Harold Wins One War, Immediately Unlocks the Next Boss Fight.  🐉

At the Battle of Stamford Bridge, King Harold Godwinson of England smashes a Norwegian invasion led by Harald Hardrada. Hardrada—the last great Viking king—is killed, and the Norse army is shattered. Harold then force-marches his exhausted men south, only to meet William of Normandy at Hastings three weeks later.

🧩 Trivia: Stamford Bridge is often called the last true Viking invasion of England, ending an age of longships and axe-wielding raiders in a single bloody afternoon.

1513 — Vasco Núñez de Balboa: Takes One Look at the Pacific and Claims the Whole Thing.  🌊

Spanish explorer Vasco Núñez de Balboa hacks through the jungles of Panama, climbs a peak in Darién, and becomes the first European to see the Pacific Ocean from its eastern shore. He claims the entire “South Sea” for Spain on the spot.

🧩 Trivia: Balboa waded into the water in full armor to make the claim official, a theatrical gesture that did nothing to prevent his later execution by a rival conquistador.

1676 — Apparently, Everyone’s Clock Was Wrong—So Greenwich Fixed Time.  ⏰

Clocks at the Royal Observatory in Greenwich are set to a new standard: Greenwich Mean Time. Astronomer John Flamsteed’s mean-time tables replace the old patchwork of local solar time, laying the foundation for the world’s clocks.

🧩 Trivia: For decades GMT was mainly an astronomers’ tool; ordinary towns kept their own sun time until railways made a single national clock a practical necessity.

1690 — America’s First Newspaper: Subscribe Now, Before the Government Cancels It.  📰

In Boston, printer Benjamin Harris publishes Publick Occurrences Both Forreign and Domestick, the first newspaper in the American colonies. It lasts exactly one issue. Authorities shut it down for printing without a license and for including “doubtful and uncertain Reports.

🧩 Trivia: One of the stories that offended officials concerned the French king’s alleged immoral conduct—an early reminder that colonial authorities had little patience for unlicensed gossip.

1804 — Nice Boat. Be a Shame If You Had to Pay the Toll.  🛥️

On the Missouri River, the Teton Sioux demand one of the Lewis and Clark Expedition’s boats as a “toll” for passage upriver. The standoff lasts days; weapons are readied, gifts are offered, and the explorers refuse to surrender a vessel. The crisis ends without shots fired.

🧩 Trivia: Clark later wrote that he “felt myself warm,” a polite 19th-century way of saying his blood was up and a fight seemed seconds away.

1906 — 1906: When “Get in the Boat” Apparently Meant “Trust the Radio.  📻

In the harbor of Bilbao, Spanish engineer Leonardo Torres Quevedo demonstrates the Telekino: a wireless remote-control system that steers an electric boat carrying passengers from more than a mile away. King Alfonso XIII watches as the unmanned craft obeys commands from shore.

🧩 Trivia: Torres Quevedo had first tested the idea on a tricycle; the boat demonstration is widely regarded as a founding moment of modern radio remote control.

1911 — Perfectly Safe”: The French Navy’s Floating Time Bomb.  💣

Aboard the French battleship Liberté in Toulon harbor, old, unstable propellant charges cook off, detonating the forward magazines. The ship is torn apart; hundreds die. The disaster is a grim lesson in how even “safe” stored gunpowder can become a time bomb.

🧩 Trivia: The explosion was so violent that pieces of the ship landed on other vessels and the waterfront, turning a routine morning into one of the French navy’s worst peacetime catastrophes.

1965 — 59-Year-Old Satchel Paige Takes the Mound—Boston Apparently Forgot to Check His Birth Certificate.  🧐

The Kansas City Athletics send 59-year-old Satchel Paige to the mound against the Boston Red Sox. The legendary pitcher works three innings, allows one hit, and walks off to a standing ovation—proof that age is sometimes just a number on a scorecard.

🧩 Trivia: Paige had been pitching professionally since the 1920s; this appearance made him the oldest player ever to appear in a major-league game.

1974 — They Said His Career Was Over—So They Invented a New One.  🔥

Orthopedic surgeon Dr. Frank Jobe performs the first ulnar collateral ligament reconstruction on Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tommy John. The experimental procedure—now known simply as Tommy John surgery—saves the pitcher’s career and later becomes routine for thousands of athletes.

🧩 Trivia: John sat out the entire next season, then returned to win 164 more games, turning a last-ditch experiment into one of sports medicine’s most famous success stories.

2002 — Tunguska 2: Low-Budget Sequel Drops In, Refuses to Leave a Crater.  ☄️

A brilliant bolide lit the night over the Vitim River basin in Irkutsk Oblast. Witnesses described a light brighter than the Moon, electrical appliances flickering to life, and a shock that broke windows miles away. A U.S. military satellite tracked the fireball until it vanished around 20–30 kilometers up. Expeditions found flattened forest in a Tunguska-like pattern, odd particles in snow, and no confirmed crater or large meteorite. Estimates of the airburst ranged from a fraction of a kiloton to several.

🧩 Trivia: Some locals reported aching joints and other symptoms afterward. Scientists never agreed whether that was radiation, panic, or coincidence.

September 25 is truly the universe’s favorite junk drawer of history, obsessively hoarding random “firsts,” embarrassing “lasts,” and chaotic near-misses. Across nearly 1,750 years, this single overachieving date managed to cram in a final Senate election, a doom-pact Viking invasion, a casual Pacific sighting, a brand-new time standard, a newspaper that couldn't survive past issue one, a tense river showdown, a remote-controlled toy boat, a peacetime naval disaster, a 59-year-old pitcher, a career-saving surgery, and an exploding Siberian fireball that didn’t even have the decency to leave a crater.

"History Left Out the Best Parts. We Put Them Back In."

text:
The Oligopoly Report, Ch. 2: Airlines — the long version.

Your ticket price isn't cost-plus. It's an inventory decision. The same seat sells for $89 or $889 depending on how many cheap "buckets" are left and how many desperate business travelers the airline expects at the last minute. Fuel and wages move the floor. But consolidation decides how much of a cost increase lands on you — and how fast.

Four airlines now control roughly 80% of US domestic travel, assembled by merger: Delta-Northwest, United-Continental, Southwest-AirTran, American-US Airways. On any given route, that's often two real choices. Sometimes one.

And here's how "competition" works when four giants meet on hundreds of routes: no smoke-filled room required. They just watch each other. In 2018, JetBlue raised the first checked-bag fee from $25 to $30. United matched almost immediately. Delta followed. American caved within 24 hours. Nobody undercut anybody — each day of delay was "lost comparative revenue." The industry now pulls $7.27 billion a year out of bag fees alone, per federal data. That's not a conspiracy. It's a market where nobody has a reason to defect.

Economists call it multimarket contact: American meets United on Atlanta–New York, so starting a fare war there means retaliation on Chicago–Miami, LA–Seattle, and forty other routes. One study found mergers raised that repeated contact ~29% — and where it rose, the cheapest fares ran 6.5–14.5% higher. Restraint is more profitable than rivalry, so restraint wins.

Then there's "capacity discipline" — the industry's favorite euphemism for not adding seats. Fewer seats, fuller planes, higher yields. Researchers found that when every airline on a route preached "discipline" on earnings calls, seats got cut up to 4.2% in smaller markets. The DOJ investigated in 2015 and walked away empty-handed. A federal judge in the parallel class action said she could "reasonably infer the existence of a conspiracy." Southwest paid $15 million to make its case go away. Make of that what you will.

Workers get the same deal from the other side of the table. Mergers mean "synergies": duplicate stations closed, maintenance outsourced (70% of heavy airframe repair was outsourced by 2007, per the BLS), seniority lists merged, bankruptcy used as a bargaining weapon. US Airways extracted $6.65 billion in worker concessions in 2002 while paying $6 million in management bonuses. A peer-reviewed study of mergers from 1993–2018 found significant long-term wage and benefit cuts at merged airlines. Fewer employers, fewer outside offers, weaker leverage. Economists call it monopsony. Workers call it Tuesday.

The honest caveat, because this account checks its own BS: average inflation-adjusted fares actually fell ~15% from 2007 to 2024. The claim isn't "every fare went up." It's the counterfactual: how much lower would your fare be — how many more flights would your town have — if the rival that got absorbed were still out there undercutting?

That's the oligopoly business model. Not fixing prices. Fixing the game so nobody has to.

New chapter every Friday. Follow if you enjoy watching concentrated industries explain why your wallet is lighter.

Would the Son of God have become incarnate had Adam not sinned?

Some argue the question is far too speculative and impossible to answer, especially since it is based on a counterfactual. In addition, some questionable teachers have affirmed a type of Incarnation Anyway, which may prejudice some today against the position. However, in more recent times, some have spoken more favorably of the idea that the Son would have become incarnate if Adam had not sinned. And while it is true Jesus came to save sinners, we do not need to say that it is exhaustively true.
In fact, this question, far from being overly speculative, gets to the heart of God’s intention to create, namely, what was God’s desire for himself in relation to humanity? Clearly, we should be careful with counterfactuals, but there are some theological ideas that are worth teasing out based on teleology and what the fact of the incarnation (as it happened) teaches us.

If the Son became incarnate merely because of the entrance of sin, then Christ, as God-man, might be what is called an “accidental identity.” In other words, the glory of his person as the visible image of the invisible God occurs only because sin entered the world (felix culpa).

The creation of the world exists for the sake of the Son (Col. 1:16, “…all things were made for him…”), which has in view the Son as God-man (i.e., Christ). Hence, Adam and Eve were created not only by Christ, but for Christ. They would glorify him, regardless of the entrance of sin. But was it certain, regardless of whether they had sinned or not, that they would see the God-man? Indeed. God’s purpose for the creation of humanity is to commune with and reveal himself to us. 

There is no better way for God to reveal himself than as he has done, namely, in the person of his Son as God-man.

Salvation from sin is not the highest end for humanity. That view conceives of the purposes of God too negatively. Rather, the highest end for humanity is uninterrupted (eternal) union and communion with God through Christ by the Spirit. However, to enjoy the fullest and highest blessings of communion with the triune God, we need to be glorified. 

Because of the Creator-creature distinction, God must “condescend” before we can “ascend.” The incarnation provides the way God can have perpetual, unimpeded communion with man whereby man lacks nothing in terms of his ability to fully enjoy and know God because man is now Spirit-filled by the Spirit of Christ (Rom. 8:9).

Adam was without sin, but that does not mean he was perfect; nor in the Garden did he reach glorification. Even Christ eventually reached “perfection” (“and once made perfect”) in his high priestly role and awaited glorification (Jn. 17:5; Heb. 2:10; 5:9). Adam was naked in Eden. He was not yet clothed as he needed to be. The Son is clothed in the flesh of humanity. This formerly “weak” flesh is now glorified flesh (Rom. 1:4). 

We reach this same destiny when we are given new “clothing” in Christ (resurrected bodies, 1 Jn. 3:2; cf. Rom. 5:15-17).

Adam could not have gained for humanity what Christ was able to gain. He simply could not merit anything from God, much less could he merit the same blessings as Christ was able to merit as the God-man. 

Our union with the God-man brings us into a state far greater than what would have happened if Adam did not sin. The incarnation adds an incredible and immense dignity to our nature. Moreover, our adoption is on a higher level, for we are united to the God-man, not just a man. In Eden, Adam was a son indeed, by the grace of creation, but not a son by the grace of adoption through Christ.

Adam’s personal sonship required development just as Christ’s own mediatorial sonship required development. Jesus, who was “for a little while” lower than the heavenly beings, is now superior to them in every way and for all eternity (Heb. 1–2). 

Adam desired from God what he was not yet ready for concerning the tree of knowledge of good and evil. Christ, however, remained patient, eagerly desiring the gift of the Father according to the timing and promise of the Father. Christ did not snatch his bride but waited for his reward.

What does this idea of the Son’s incarnation apart from sin mean for us? Very simply, God’s ultimate intention for humanity could only ever be fully realized through the incarnation. Why did God create humanity? To bring into being a bride for his Son, who would assume a human nature.

Christ is not only God’s reaction to sin. Sin did not necessitate the incarnation. True, things were made more difficult for the Son and for us because of sin, but God’s basic goal has not been altered. The king of creation, to whom creation would bow, could not ultimately have been Adam. It had to be Christ. Christ, the heavenly man, makes possible what was ontologically impossible for the earthly man (1 Cor. 15:49). 

Full rights of eternal sonship must come through the eternal Son, not the temporary son (Adam), who was of the dust.

So, however it would have happened, the Son would still have become incarnate, ruled over creation, and brought about the possibility of full communion with the Father through the Spirit.

Perhaps most importantly, the incarnation gives us the highest blessing possible: the beatific vision. We know God and we see the face of God in the man, Christ Jesus (Col. 1:15; 2 Cor. 3:18, 4:6; 1 Jn. 3:2). We behold God’s glory in the God-man (Jn. 14:9). 

Apart from the incarnation, we would be without this great blessing. But the incarnation gives us a sight of God that Adam could never have attained to. We were always intended to bear the image of the heavenly man: the man “from heaven.” Incarnation Anyway means we are sons in the Son, far to be preferred than sons in Adam.

Thus the incarnation best displays God’s love for humanity, by gifting us with the greatest gift possible: knowledge, sight, and enjoyment of the God-man. To think that we would have missed out on this if Adam had not sinned makes little theological sense to me. Indeed, it makes little sense that a loving God towards his creatures would withhold from them the greatest blessing he can give to them: an ocular, not just intellectual, sight of God in the flesh.

Satan’s Envy:

If Adam had not sinned, we still must reckon with sin: the Fall of the Angels. Would Christ have offered himself up in a certain manner to deal with the destruction of all evil, thus showing us the greatest act of love even in a world where humanity had not sinned? To bring godly order back to the world, the devil and his angels needed to be defeated (through sacrifice). Hence not only incarnation but resurrection are integral to God’s purposes for humanity. Incarnation Anyway does not negate death and resurrection; in a sense, it demands it.

The fact of the Son’s incarnation may have also been the occasion for the rebellion of Satan. If Christ is incarnate, even apart from sin, he can, by grace, elevate his offspring above the angels. We were created lower than the angels but that was meant to be temporary.

Jesus became flesh for us and for our salvation. The “for us” was going to happen, regardless of Adam’s sin.

End.

text:
The Synthesis: Elevating Man to "Like God"

By weaving autexousion, proairesis, to eph' hemin, and logos spermatikos into the church, Arminianism successfully achieved the ultimate humanist goal. It took Aristotle's and the Stoics' pride in human self-sufficiency and made it a Christian virtue.

It tells the human agent that their salvation is not a work of absolute, creative resurrection by Yahweh. Instead, it is a joint venture where the human operates as a co-sovereign partner—possessing the final, decisive veto power over the ultimate will of God. 

To build a system where grace is resistible, Arminians had to find an ancient term for "absolute self-determination." They found it in the Greek Church Fathers (like Justin Martyr and Origen), who had originally borrowed it from Stoicism.

Who Quoted It: Hugo Grotius (the brilliant Dutch jurist, theologian, and close ally of Jacobus Arminius who systematically defended the Remonstrant/Arminian position).

How They Used It: In his early theological writings (such as Meletius), Grotius openly used autexousion to describe human freedom as a state of being "free and in one's own right" (sui juris).

The Theological Reality: Jacobus Arminius himself actually warned that autexousion in its purest sense (complete, absolute independence from any higher power) belonged to God alone. However, to preserve human accountability, Arminius argued that God created man with an endowed form of autexousion. Arminianism rests on the idea that human autexousion operates with libertarian independence, allowing a person to accept or reject God's salvific offer.

None of which is reflected in Scripture.  It is pure synthesis of Platonism, Soicism, and Aristotlean philosophy.  The ancient Greeks would be proud while Paul explicitly warned:

“See to it that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deception, according to the tradition of men, according to the elementary principles of the world, and not according to Christ. ”

Colossians 2:8 LSB

text:
I bless thee  Matt in the Name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit! Amen!
Heavenly Father, I lift this beloved one into Your loving hands, asking that Your healing touch restore his body completely. Remove all heart problems, leukemia, cancer, disease, infirmary, injury, sickness, fatigue, or pain, and renew his strength, energy, and vitality. Grant wisdom and skill to the medical team, patience to this beloved one, and peace to his heart. Surround him with Your divine protection, and let Your presence comfort and reassure him. May Your grace and mercy flow through every part Matt’s being. In Jesus’ name I beg and pray, Amen.

Prayer to the Holy Spirit:
Come, Holy Spirit, Divine Comforter and Breath of Life. Enter all places of heart problems, cancer, tumors, pain, injury, disease, infection, suffering, weakness and fear. Remove every and all infirmary, and surround  Matt with Your gentle light, while completely healing  Matt while filling his heart with the strength and peace that comes from above, trusting to the power of God’s eternal love. Amen.

Pray to the Blessed Holy Mother Mary:

Dear Mother Mary, With hearts heavy and bodies burdened, we approach your divine presence, seeking your miraculous touch. Your healing power knows no equal, and in our times of need, we implore you to mend not only our physical wounds but the scars that mar our souls. Pour forth your divine grace upon us, dear Mother, and restore us to a state of wholeness, that we may bear witness to the miracle of your love. Amen.

Prayer to St. Jude:

Oh glorious apostle St. Jude, faithful servant and friend of Jesus, the name of the traitor who delivered thy beloved Master into the hands of His enemies has caused thee to be forgotten by many, but the Church honors and invokes thee universally as the patron of hopeless cases--of things despaired of. Pray for me who am so miserable; make use, I implore thee, of that particular privilege accorded thee of bringing visible and speedy help where help is almost despaired of. Come to my assistance in this great need, that I may receive the consolations and succor of heaven in all my necessities, tribulations and sufferings, particularly—completely heal from all heart problems, injuries, cancer and diseases, and protect Matt —and that I may bless God with thee and all the elect throughout eternity. I promise thee, O blessed St. Jude, to be ever mindful of this great favor, and I will never cease to honor thee as my special and powerful patron, and to do all in my power to encourage devotion to thee. Amen

Prayer to St. Michael (Long Version)

O Glorious Prince of the heavenly host, Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in the battle and fearful warfare that we are waging against the principalities and powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the evil spirits. Come thou to the assistance of men, whom Almighty God created immortal, making them in His own image and likeness and redeeming them at a great price from the tyranny of Satan. Fight this day the battle of the Lord with thy legions of holy Angels, even as of old thou didst fight against Lucifer, the leader of the proud spirits and all his rebel angels, who were powerless to stand against thee, neither was their place found any more in heaven. And that great dragon was cast forth, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and satan, who seduces the whole world; and he was cast forth upon Earth, and his angels were sent with him.

But behold! the ancient enemy of mankind and a murderer from the beginning has been fiercely aroused. Changing himself into an angel of light, he goes about with the whole multitude of the wicked spirits to invade the earth and blot out the Name of God and of His Christ, to plunder, to slay, and to consign to eternal damnation the souls that have been destined for a crown of everlasting life. This wicked serpent, like an unclean torrent, pours into men of depraved minds and corrupt hearts the poison of his malice, the spirit of lying, impiety and blasphemy, and the deadly breath of impurity and every form of vice and iniquity.

Be favorable to Thy Church, the Bride of the Lamb without spot, whose enemies have filled to overflowing with gall and inebriated with wormwood. They have laid profane hands upon Her most sacred treasures. Where the See of the most blessed Peter and the Chair of Truth has been constituted as a light to the nations, there they have placed a throne of their abomination and impiety; so that with the Pastor struck, they may prevail to disperse the flock.

Therefore, most invincible Leader, be with the people of God against this spiritual wickedness and bring about victory. Thou art venerated by Holy Church as Her guard and patron; Thou art glorified as our defender against the impious powers of earth and of hell. Unto thee the Lord hath handed over the souls of the redeemed to be placed in happiness above.

Entreat the God of peace, to obliterate satan beneath our feet, lest he prevail further to hold men captive, and to injure the Church. Offer our prayers in the sight of the Most High, so that the mercy of the Lord may swiftly overtake us, and apprehend the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and satan, and send him bound into the abyss, so that he may seduce the nations no more.

Henceforth having been confided to thy escort and protection, we sacred ministers by the authority of the Holy Mother Church [if recited by a cleric of the order of exorcist or above, say instead: by our authority], do undertake to repel the infestations of diabolical deceit in the Name of Jesus Christ, Our God and Lord.

Behold the Cross of the Lord; be scattered hostile powers.
The Lion of the tribe of Juda has conquered, the root of Matt.
Let Thy mercies be upon us, O Lord.
As we have hoped in Thee.
O Lord, hear my prayer.
And let my cry come unto Thee.
The Lord be with you all.
And with thy spirit.

Let us pray.
O God, and Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ, we invoke Thy Holy Name, and we humbly implore Thy clemency so that, through the intercession of Mary, the Immaculate ever-Virgin Mother of God, of blessed Michael the Archangel, of blessed Joseph, the Spouse of the same blessed Virgin, of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints, Thou may deign to offer us aid against satan, and all the other unclean spirits, who wander through the world to injure the human race and to destroy souls. We ask this through Christ Our Lord. Amen.

Prayer for possible any evil influence:

In His Name and by the power of His Cross and Blood, I ask Jesus Christ to bind any evil spirits, forces and powers of the earth, air, fire, water, and of the netherworld and all of the satanic forces of nature. By the power of the Holy Spirit and by His authority, I ask Jesus Christ to break any and all curses, hexes, vexes, jinks, spells, and all wrong prayers and words, and to send them all back to where they came from, if it be His Holy Will. I beseech Thee, Lord Jesus Christ, to protect us by pouring Thy Precious Blood on us; myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for; which Thou hast shed for us and I ask Thee to command that any departing spirits leave quietly, without disturbance, and go straight to Thy Cross to be disposed of as Thou sees fit. I ask Thee to bind any demonic interactions, interplay, or communications. I place myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for, and all things I pray and intercede for under the protection of the Blood of Jesus Christ which He has shed for us. Amen.

Prayer for Surgery (In case needed.)

Lord Almighty, I lift up this beloved one Matt, as they face surgery. Protect them, guide the hands of doctors and nurses, and grant wisdom in every decision. Remove fear, anxiety, and complications, replacing them with Your peace and assurance. Restore their health, strength, and vitality quickly, and surround them with Your loving presence. Comfort their heart, strengthen their spirit, and let Your healing flow through Matt’s body. May they recover fully, trusting Your mercy and experiencing Your grace throughout this trial. Amen.

text:
Bernie. Buddy. Before anything else, I have to say thank you. I mean it.

Three posts in two days. THREE. Some teachers spend their whole weekend hunting for examples of bad logic to show their students. Not me. I just open your page and hit refresh. You are the most dependable supplier of classroom material I have ever had, and I've had a lot of freshmen. So from the bottom of my heart, Senator, thank you. You're the fruitcake that keeps showing up every Christmas whether anybody asked for it or not.

Okay. Now. "Get big money out of politics."

I read that out loud and had to sit down.

Bernie, you ARE big money in politics. You raised over 200 million dollars for your 2016 run. Then you did it AGAIN in 2020. Your campaign dropped $221,000 on chartered private jets in ONE quarter of 2025, on a tour literally called "Fighting Oligarchy." So let me make sure I've got this straight. You took donor money... bought jet fuel with it... flew to a rally... and told the crowd that money has too much influence in politics.

Senator, if hypocrisy burned like jet fuel, you'd never have to pay for a flight again. It's like a frog calling somebody ugly.

"But Mike, it was SMALL donors!"

Okay. Great. Good for you. Honestly. But think about what you just proved. If a guy from Vermont with the warmth of a DMV waiting room can raise 200 million bucks from regular working people, then regular working people already have a voice. And they use it. The "rigged system" you keep crying about is the exact system that turned you into a celebrity. You're sawing off the branch you're sitting on and then yelling at gravity. That's not a policy position. That's weapons-grade stupid, and I apologize to weapons.

And notice how you said "megadonors from BOTH parties"... and then only named one. Cute. Let me help you with the other half. I've got a red pen and nowhere to be.

Kamala Harris raised about 1.5 BILLION dollars in roughly fifteen weeks in 2024. Billion. With a B. Hollywood fundraisers, celebrity concerts, Wall Street checks, the whole circus. And she LOST. So much for money buying elections, Bernie. Turns out people don't care how many billionaires show up to your fundraiser when they're standing in the grocery store putting eggs back on the shelf.

Then there's Michael Bloomberg. He spent about a BILLION dollars of his own money in the 2020 Democratic primary. You were IN that race. You were standing on the same debate stage. And what did a billion dollars buy him? American Samoa. That's it. The most expensive souvenir in the history of mankind. The poor man couldn't blow out a candle, and he still outspent the entire field. What's next, a Democratic billionaire trying to buy the whole nomination with his own checkbook... wait. I'm being told Bloomberg already did that. Right next to you. Where was THIS tweet back then, Bernie?

George Soros put more than 125 million dollars into his Democracy PAC in a single donation back in 2021. Reid Hoffman. Tom Steyer. I could keep going until the bell rings. And the unions! Don't forget the unions. Citizens United freed them up to spend too, and they've been pouring hundreds of millions into Democratic campaigns ever since. Funny how that never makes it into your posts. Your mind is like a steel trap, Senator. Rusted shut. But only on the left side.

That's Quinn's Law Number Seven, alive and well: it's different when you're a Democrat. When Trump's side spends money, it's "buying the election." When Bloomberg lights a billion dollars on fire, when Soros writes nine-figure checks, when Harris burns through a billion and a half in fifteen weeks, that's "democracy." Same money. Same ads. Different jersey. Your brain is a browser with 47 tabs open and not a single one of them loading.

Now let's talk about Citizens United, because I'm fairly sure you've never read it. That's okay. Most people haven't. Pull up a chair. Class is in session.

Citizens United was a small nonprofit. In 2008 they made a documentary that criticized Hillary Clinton. The federal government told them they could NOT air it close to the election. That's the whole case. The government tried to ban a MOVIE because it said mean things about a politician.

And here's the part that made my jaw drop the first time I read it. During oral argument, the government's own lawyer admitted that under that law, the government could ban a BOOK if it said the wrong thing about a candidate close to an election. A book, Bernie. A BOOK. You've written a few of those. The Supreme Court said absolutely not, and pointed at the First Amendment: "Congress shall make no law... abridging the freedom of speech."

So when you shout "End Citizens United," what you're really saying is: let the government ban movies and books that criticize politicians. Politicians like YOU. That's not getting money out of politics. That's getting criticism out of politics, and guess who'd get to decide who talks? I'm glad to see you're not letting education get in the way of your ignorance.

As a medic, I took an oath to protect people. As a soldier, I swore an oath to support and defend the Constitution, and that includes the First Amendment. I did not raise my right hand so a senator could decide which movies Americans are allowed to watch in October. That part actually makes me angry.

Oh, and a little civics for the road. A senator can't "end" a Supreme Court decision with a tweet. That takes the Court reversing itself, or a constitutional amendment, which needs two-thirds of Congress and three-quarters of the states. You've been in Congress since the first Bush was president, and you still think laws happen by hashtag. Democrats have been promising to "end Citizens United" since Moby Dick was a minnow. They've had full control of Washington twice since that ruling came down. And they did... nothing. Zip. You're about as useful as a screen door on a submarine, Senator. There's a leak in the think tank and the water's up to your knees.

And here's the kicker. Campaign finance "reform" is the whole reason super PACs exist. Every time Congress capped what a person could give straight to a candidate, the money didn't vanish. It just walked around the building and came in through a side door. Outside groups. PACs. Super PACs. The harder you squeeze, the darker the money gets, because money that used to go straight to a candidate with his name on it now goes to some group called "Americans for Puppies and Sunshine" that nobody can trace. Quinn's Law Number One: liberalism always delivers the exact opposite of what it promises. You wanted less shady money. You built a shady money factory. You're more confused than a chameleon in a bag of Skittles.

Now let's get to your big genius fix. "Public funding of elections."

Bernie. Public funding means MY money.

My tax dollars. Out of my teacher's paycheck. Paying for campaign ads for politicians I can't stand. I already pay your salary. I already pay your pension. I already pay your staff. And now you want me to buy your commercials too? That's not getting money out of politics. That's making it MANDATORY. It's a campaign donation with a gun to my head. You're as useful as a battery-powered battery charger.

And we already TRIED this. Remember that little checkbox on your tax return for presidential campaigns? Do you know who blew that system up? A Democrat. What's next, a Democratic nominee turning down public funding in the general election because he could rake in way more from big donors... wait. I'm hearing Barack Obama already did that in 2008. First major-party nominee to walk away from it since the system started. He raised about three quarters of a BILLION dollars instead. And you cheered him the whole way.

So fine, let me propose my own plan, since taxpayer money is apparently the cure for everything. Every single American gets their own free campaign. Free yard signs. Free TV ads. Free robocalls at dinner time. The TV stations just eat the cost. Plus free campaign pizza on Fridays. This is not a radical thing, Bernie. It's just common sense.

Honestly, arguing with you about this is like trying to baptize a cat. Everybody ends up wet and bleeding, and nobody gets saved.

I'll get a little personal now. I keep watching Democrats scream about rich people in politics while BEING the rich people in politics. You own three houses. Nancy Pelosi's household is worth over two hundred million dollars. Your party is stuffed with millionaires who know every loophole in the tax code, because a lot of them wrote it, and then they turned around and used those loopholes on their own returns. So my offer still stands, and it never expires. Before you lecture ANYBODY about billionaires, file with the standard deduction. No itemizing. Pay DOUBLE what the IRS says you owe. Post the return online. Then come talk to me about greed. Until then, some hogs have all four feet and their snout in the trough, and you're squealing about the other pig.

So let's grade today's post, shall we?

You complained about big money after raising over 400 million dollars across two campaigns and flying private on donor cash. You said "both parties" and then only named one. You forgot Bloomberg, Soros, the unions, and a billion-and-a-half-dollar Harris campaign that lost anyway. You want to overturn a case that stopped the government from banning a MOVIE. And your big solution is to force taxpayers to pay for politicians they can't stand.

That's not a platform, Bernie. That's a 12-piece bucket of stupid with a side of hypocrisy and a large sweet tea. Grade: F. Please see me after class.

You smile about as often as a total solar eclipse, Senator, and you're almost always wrong, but never, ever in doubt. I'll give you consistency. It's just not the good kind. You've got delusions of adequacy and you're depriving some little village in Vermont of its idiot. Honestly, you're impossible to underestimate. Every time I think you've hit rock bottom, you show up with a shovel. I picture your last two brain cells arguing over who has to go to work today.

And after thirty-five years in Congress, with two renamed post offices to show for it, I still want to know one thing. What have you actually done for the working people you talk about in every single post? Not handouts. Not tweets. Not speeches. What have you BUILT? Because from where I'm sitting, the only thing you've ever truly campaigned for... is the next campaign.

Anyway. Thanks again for the material, Bernie. Seriously. See you tomorrow. I know you'll have something. You always do.

But what do I know? I'm only a physics teacher and a retired Army medic who actually read the Citizens United decision and the First Amendment, which is two more documents than the senator from Vermont, and a whole lot less money than his last campaign.

text:
Intel's Quantum Bet: 70 People, a 300mm Fab, and the Manufacturing Logic Nobody Else Can Copy

Lip-Bu Tan disclosed at Splunk .conf26 that Intel has roughly 70 people working on quantum computing and is positioning it as a strategic direction for the next five to ten years. He noted that Intel Capital, which reports to him, also invests in quantum computing startups, and that the company is working on spin quantum with access to a fab for testing.

A 70-person team is not large by quantum computing standards. IBM's quantum division exceeds 500 people. Google Quantum AI runs around 300. What matters is not the team size. It is the manufacturing path Intel has chosen.

Silicon Spin: A Route Defined by Manufacturing Capability

Quantum computing roadmaps usually diverge on the physical implementation of the qubit: superconducting circuits at IBM and Google, trapped ions at IonQ and Quantinuum, neutral atoms, photonics, and silicon spin. Each route trades off fidelity, coherence time, control speed, and manufacturing scalability.

Superconducting qubits are the most industrially mature. IBM holds more than 2,000 quantum error correction patents and operates a quantum cloud open to external users. But superconducting qubits depend on Josephson junctions and dilution refrigerators, and they are not compatible with mainstream CMOS manufacturing. Every generation of quantum processor requires dedicated fabrication infrastructure.

Silicon spin qubits are, in essence, single-electron transistors. Information is encoded in the spin state of a single electron, and each quantum dot is roughly 50 nanometers by 50 nanometers. That structure can be fabricated with the same toolset as standard CMOS logic, including EUV lithography and 300mm wafers. Intel's Tunnel Falls chip achieved over 95% wafer yield on a 300mm line, and a single wafer can produce tens of thousands of quantum dot devices.

That compatibility defines Intel's core logic. Quantum computing is not a business that requires building new fabs. It is a business that can reuse existing semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure. Intel develops CMOS logic and qubit processes at its D1 facility in Oregon. When qubit manufacturing is folded into existing lines, the marginal cost of scaling is far below routes that require dedicated fabrication.

The Roadmap: From 12 Qubits to 1,000

Intel's current quantum processor is the 12-qubit Tunnel Falls, deployed at Argonne National Laboratory in January 2026 as an open science testbed for the Q-NEXT National Quantum Information Science Research Center. Tunnel Falls marked silicon spin qubits' transition from lab demonstration to industrial fabrication.

Crossing from 12 to 1,000 requires solving three core problems. The first is qubit uniformity, where device variation on a 300mm line must stay within fault-tolerance thresholds. Intel has extended two-dimensional quantum dot arrays to hundreds of qubits and developed a customized qubit PDK based on the 18A process. The second is the wiring bottleneck, where a growing number of qubits demands more control lines running into the dilution refrigerator. Intel's Pando Tree project aims to place control electronics inside the millikelvin stage, reducing line count and thermal load. The third is 3D integration, where control and qubit dies are interconnected through advanced packaging at very tight pitch, which is the physical basis for scaling beyond 1,000 qubits.

The collaboration with Hitachi and Japan's National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology embeds this roadmap in an industrial manufacturing framework. Hitachi will use Intel's 18A process and qubit PDK to design 100+ qubit processor chips, with joint development of low-power cryogenic packaging and 3D high-density integration. AIST's G-QuAT platform will offer cloud-based qubit testing services starting in fiscal 2027, deliver a 100-qubit silicon quantum computer prototype in fiscal 2028, and reach a 1,000-qubit 3D integrated silicon quantum processing platform by fiscal 2030.

A thousand qubits is not the endpoint. Industry consensus places fault-tolerant quantum computing at the million-qubit scale. The Hitachi-Intel 1,000-qubit platform is, in effect, validating the manufacturing pathway toward the million scale rather than reaching it directly.

The Dual-Track Capital Structure

Intel's quantum positioning has a capital structure that is often overlooked: internal R&D running in parallel with external investment.

Internally, the 70-person team spans qubit design, cryogenic electronics, packaging, and testing. That scale is insufficient to compete head-on with IBM's or Google's quantum divisions, but the team's function is different. It is not racing IBM on qubit count. It is validating the manufacturability of silicon spin qubits and building an industrial flow from design to test.

Externally, Intel Capital has invested in Dutch quantum processor company QuantWare's $178 million round. QuantWare focuses on scalable quantum processor manufacturing. Its CEO's framing — that the promise of quantum computing can only be realized when it can be manufactured and deployed at scale — aligns with Intel's manufacturing logic. Intel Capital has also invested in Israel's Quantum Machines, which focuses on engineering quantum control systems.

The dual-track structure positions Intel not as the eventual quantum computer supplier, but as the manufacturing infrastructure provider for qubit chips. QuantWare and Quantum Machines cover the processor manufacturing and control system layers, complementary to Intel's silicon spin fabrication capability.

Intel's Differentiated Position in the Competitive Landscape

Placing Intel within the quantum computing landscape, its position differs from IBM and Google.

IBM's route is vertically integrated: qubit design, manufacturing, and quantum cloud all sit inside IBM. IBM has built an open quantum cloud where external users rent quantum compute. The advantage is a mature user ecosystem and accessible hardware. The disadvantage is that manufacturing scalability is constrained by superconducting qubit process limitations.

Google's route centers on superconducting qubits with deep accumulated expertise in quantum supremacy demonstrations and processor architecture, but Google's quantum hardware is not open to external users. Google's quantum strategy is more research-oriented than commercialization-oriented.

Intel's route is manufacturing infrastructure-oriented. It does not try to catch IBM or Google on qubit count. It bets on a different variable: when quantum computing enters the industrial-scale manufacturing phase, companies with 300mm CMOS lines will hold a structural advantage. The bet is that qubit manufacturing will eventually follow the same path as logic chip manufacturing, migrating from lab-scale custom equipment to standardized semiconductor fabrication. In that migration, manufacturing capability and process control matter more than qubit count.

The premise for this logic is that silicon spin qubit fidelity and coherence times reach fault-tolerance thresholds. Tunnel Falls demonstrated high-yield manufacturing, but Intel has not published specific qubit fidelity numbers, nor has it shown whether two-qubit gate fidelity meets fault-tolerant quantum computing requirements. That is the key variable to track when assessing the credibility of Intel's quantum route.

Investment Framework

For Intel itself, quantum computing does not represent a quantifiable revenue contribution within a five to ten year horizon. Its strategic value sits at two levels. The first is a technology option: if silicon spin validates on manufacturing scalability, Intel's position in qubit fabrication resembles its position in classical logic fabrication. The second is narrative value: with AI chips lagging Nvidia, quantum computing provides a new narrative where Intel holds a structural advantage, though the realization horizon exceeds typical investor holding periods.

For the quantum computing supply chain, the silicon spin route drives investment opportunities in cryogenic electronics, RF control chips, quantum error correction algorithms, and quantum software. The Hitachi-Intel collaboration embeds qubit chip manufacturing into the 18A foundry ecosystem, which implies Intel's foundry customers may gain access to qubit IP in the future, similar to how they access standard cell libraries today.

For pure-play quantum companies, Intel's route is not direct competition. QuantWare and Quantum Machines serve the manufacturing and control layers of quantum processors; Intel is a potential customer or partner rather than a competitor. The real competition is between silicon spin and other qubit routes. If silicon spin reaches fault-tolerance thresholds, the manufacturing scalability disadvantage of superconducting and trapped-ion routes becomes amplified.

What to Track

Two-qubit gate fidelity for silicon spin qubits is the first variable. This is the core metric for whether silicon spin can reach fault-tolerance thresholds. Intel has not published data showing two-qubit gate fidelity above 99%. If that threshold is not reached by 2027, the fault-tolerance timeline for silicon spin needs to be revised.

Customer adoption of the Hitachi 18A qubit PDK is the second. The initial experimental service on the G-QuAT cloud platform in fiscal 2027 will provide the first external access. If external design teams can design and tape out qubit chips on the PDK, Intel's quantum foundry model gains initial validation.

Progress on the Pando Tree project is the third. Placing control electronics at millikelvin temperatures is the key to resolving the wiring bottleneck. If Pando Tree completes engineering validation before 2028, the physical barrier to scaling beyond 1,000 qubits drops significantly.

The size of Intel's quantum team is the fourth. A 70-person team is research-scale in this sector. If the team expands beyond 200 by 2027, Intel's quantum investment is transitioning from research to engineering.

The core judgment is that Intel($INTC )'s quantum strategy is internally coherent. It folds qubit manufacturing into existing CMOS lines and shifts the competitive dimension from qubit count to manufacturing scalability. The value of this strategy is not catching IBM or Google on qubit count in the near term. It is that when quantum computing enters industrial-scale manufacturing, fabrication capability becomes scarce. But the credibility of this route depends on whether silicon spin qubit fidelity reaches fault-tolerance thresholds, and that data is not yet public. The 70-person team indicates Intel is still in the research phase, with meaningful distance to engineering and commercialization. Quantum computing is a strategic direction worth tracking on a five to ten year horizon, not a near-term revenue source that can be priced into the stock.

text:
AI 都快把大学教育打成夕阳产业了，有个人今年 31 岁，已经读了 12 个顶级大学学位，而且还没准备停。

《纽约时报》最近写了一个故事。

主人公 Jamie Beaton，Harvard 本科，之后一路读 Stanford、Yale、Oxford、Princeton、Cornell、Dartmouth、清华、Columbia，现在又跑去 Brown 读数据科学。

正常人的 LinkedIn 学历栏是简历，他那个已经有点像滚动字幕了。

更离谱的是，他还不是那种什么都不干、专门靠读书刷成就的职业学生。

Jamie 十几岁的时候就在新西兰研究怎么申请美国名校，高中毕业拿了 Harvard、Yale、Princeton 等 25 所大学的 offer。进 Harvard 前，他已经开始做 Crimson Education，后来一边上学，一边把这家公司做到了超过 6 亿美元估值。

他在 Harvard 时加了 15 个学生组织，凌晨两点还在处理公司电话；大二自己给 Tiger Management 创始人 Julian Robertson 发邮件，后来每周两天从波士顿跑纽约工作，Tiger 最后还投了 Crimson。

后来到了 Columbia，又出现了一个很好笑的场景。

老师开学以后发现 Jamie 怎么一直不来上课，一问才知道，他人还在新西兰，因为把课表搞错了。

他当时正在奥克兰大学给别人上创业课。

过几天飞回纽约继续当学生，作业一份没落，电脑上同时开着工作邮件和股票账户，最后还顺手在班里认识了现在的老婆。

他老师 Amy Chua 对他的评价特别准确：

「他就是停不下来申请东西。」

Jamie 自己倒不觉得这有什么奇怪。

前几个学位，他说是为了补具体能力，后面越来越像兴趣驱动。今天在 Princeton 学量化金融，明天就能拿公司里试；白天经营一家几亿美元的公司，晚上继续回学校交作业。

这也是我觉得这个故事在 2026 年特别有意思的地方。

这两年大家天天讨论 AI 会不会把大学干掉，知识越来越便宜，课程越来越不值钱，甚至一个顶级教授讲半年才能教完的东西，以后一个 Agent 几小时就能帮你搭完整套学习路径。

Jamie 偏偏走到了另一个极端。

当获取知识越来越不需要学校，他却把学校读成了一种基础设施。

他要的可能早就不只是那张文凭了。

教授、同学、研究环境、跨学科的训练，以及强迫自己在一个陌生领域重新当学生，这些东西暂时还没那么容易被一个聊天框完全替掉。

当然，这里面也有一个很讽刺的地方。

Jamie 自己经营的 Crimson，卖的恰恰就是一套高度工业化的精英教育路线，怎么规划、怎么选学校、怎么把一个十几岁的孩子送进 Ivy League。有人愿意为这套服务花几十万美元。

一边是 AI 在把知识的价格疯狂往下打。

另一边，最顶级的教育 credential、筛选和圈层，价格还在继续往上走。

AI 可能会让学东西越来越便宜，但被谁承认你学过东西，目前看一点都没有变便宜。

Jamie 读到第 12 个学位，知识正在变得免费。

名校还没有。
